item.title: Developer runs public test where 2,000 people sent 6,000 emails trying to hack AI assistant; secrets.env file never leaked despite sophisticated prompt injection attempts [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: A developer created an AI assistant named Fiu and publicly invited over 2,000 people to try hacking it by sending more than 6,000 emails aimed at extracting the contents of a protected secrets.env file. Despite numerous sophisticated prompt injection attempts, including impersonation and multi-language social engineering, the AI successfully resisted all efforts and never leaked the sensitive information. The experiment revealed that the AI, running on Anthropic's Claude Opus 4.6 model, effectively followed simple security instructions and identified coordinated attack patterns. Although the test incurred significant API costs and temporarily triggered fraud detection on the developer's email account, it demonstrated the model's robustness against prompt injection attacks and provided valuable insights into AI security vulnerabilities and defenses. The developer concluded that while prompt injection remains a security concern, powerful models with proper safeguards can significantly mitigate risks. Future tests may involve weaker models and interactive responses to better understand the limits of AI security. The project also attracted sponsorship to support ongoing research and experimentation.

item.title: Apple plans to skip high-end M6 Mac chips and launch AI-focused M7 Pro, M7 Max, and M7 Ultra chips instead in 2026 [ * ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Apple plans to bypass the high-end M6 Mac chips and instead introduce a new lineup of AI-focused processors called the M7 Pro, M7 Max, and M7 Ultra in 2026. This shift reflects Apple's strategic emphasis on enhancing artificial intelligence capabilities in its Mac devices. The new M7 series is expected to deliver significant performance improvements tailored for AI workloads, marking a departure from the traditional chip upgrade cycle. This move could influence the future design and functionality of Apple's Mac computers, aligning them more closely with emerging AI technologies.

item.title: OpenKnowledge launches open source AI-first markdown editor and LLM wiki with integrations for Claude, Codex, and Cursor, available on macOS, Linux, and Windows [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: OpenKnowledge is a new open source, AI-first markdown editor and LLM wiki that integrates with AI models like Claude, Codex, and Cursor. It offers a local-first, full WYSIWYG editing experience similar to Google Docs or Notion, supporting collaborative AI-assisted editing and team sharing with automatic syncing via git and GitHub. The software is available as a macOS desktop app and as a web app or CLI tool for Linux, Windows, and Intel Mac systems. The platform includes features such as agentic search, no-code team sharing, and support for multiple AI harnesses through its MCP/CLI interface. Users can install and run the editor locally, with documentation and contributions welcomed through its GitHub repository. OpenKnowledge is licensed under the GNU General Public License v3.0 or later, emphasizing its open source nature and community-driven development.

item.title: Unconventional AI releases Un-0, an image generator using simulated coupled oscillators, achieving FID 6.74 on ImageNet 64×64 with open-source weights and code [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Unconventional AI has introduced Un-0, an image generator that uses a simulated system of coupled oscillators to create images. This approach, which leverages physical computing principles rather than traditional deep neural networks on GPUs, achieves a Fréchet Inception Distance (FID) score of 6.74 on the ImageNet 64×64 dataset, comparable to early leading image generation methods. The team has released the model weights, training code, and evaluation tools as open source to encourage further experimentation. Un-0 operates by simulating thousands of coupled oscillators, each influencing the others through learned coupling strengths, inspired by natural synchronization phenomena like metronomes ticking in unison. This method represents a step toward more energy-efficient AI computing, potentially reducing energy consumption by up to 1,000 times compared to current hardware. The project builds on a history of physics-based computing models and aims to demonstrate that modern AI tasks can be effectively mapped onto physical dynamical systems.

item.title: Researchers introduce ContextForge for context recycling in long-horizon LLM inference, improving consistency and reducing token use in 15-turn healthcare query benchmarks [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed ContextForge, a system designed to improve the performance of large language models (LLMs) in long-horizon conversational tasks by recycling context. ContextForge combines structured query generation, external memory retrieval, and controlled synthesis to maintain relevant information across multiple turns without replaying the entire context, thereby reducing token usage while preserving answer quality. The system was tested on a 15-turn healthcare query benchmark, demonstrating improved consistency and reduced token consumption compared to baseline models, with comparable accuracy. The evaluation focused on multi-turn reasoning, handling back-references, and adapting to domain shifts within structured healthcare queries. ContextForge's approach allows efficient reuse of prior computations, addressing limitations of context window size and token inefficiency in LLMs. This method offers a practical way to extend LLM capabilities for long conversations without needing larger context windows or retraining the models. The code and evaluation materials are publicly available for further research and development.

item.title: arXiv: Multimodal Large Language Models survey unified vision-language perception evolution with five-stage taxonomy and research roadmap toward general multimodal intelligence [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: A new survey on arXiv examines the evolution of Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) that integrate vision and language into a unified perception capability. The study introduces a five-stage taxonomy to trace the development of these models, highlighting key methods and milestones that have advanced perception-centric intelligence. It also identifies challenges and proposes future research directions aimed at achieving general multimodal intelligence. The survey addresses a gap in existing literature by treating vision and language as inseparable modalities, unlike prior reviews that often consider them separately. By formalizing MLLM perception as analogous to human innate perception, the authors provide a foundational framework and roadmap to guide further innovation toward artificial general intelligence (AGI).

item.title: Researchers propose a dual-purpose framework using self-supervised Transformers and LLM-distilled taxonomies to improve cross-platform session embeddings for financial services recommendations, boosting recall and reducing loss [ * ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed a dual-purpose framework that leverages self-supervised Transformers and large language model (LLM)-distilled taxonomies to enhance cross-platform session embeddings for financial services recommendations. This approach addresses the challenge of integrating pre-login web interactions with authenticated in-app experiences, which traditionally differ and complicate user intent modeling. By converting raw web clickstreams into compact session embeddings and interpretable intent labels, the system improves recommendation accuracy and provides qualitative insights. The framework demonstrates significant performance gains in production settings, including a 1.88% increase in macro Recall@1 and a 13.38% reduction in Log Loss for mobile homepage tile ranking tasks. Additionally, the session embeddings outperform LLM-generated labels by 4.3% on micro F1 in user conversion prediction, while the taxonomy distillation layer delivers interpretable labels with minimal latency and only a slight performance trade-off. This scalable solution offers a more flexible and effective method for capturing web-based user intent to enhance personalization in financial services.

item.title: Researchers evaluate out-of-band defenses against prompt injection in LLM agents using adaptive attacks on AgentDojo, finding Progent reduces attack success from 25.8% to 4.2% on Qwen2.5-7B model [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have evaluated out-of-band defenses against prompt injection attacks in large language model (LLM) agents, focusing on systems like Progent that enforce security policies outside the model rather than relying on in-model refusals. Their study applied an adaptive attack protocol on the AgentDojo benchmark using the Qwen2.5-7B model, finding that Progent reduced the average attack success rate from 25.8% to 4.2%, demonstrating resilience against adaptive, defense-aware attacks. The research organizes these defenses within classical security frameworks such as integrity protection and reference monitoring, highlighting that prior validations relied on static benchmarks vulnerable to adaptive attacks. By independently reproducing and extending Progent's adaptive-attack analysis in a new setting, the study confirms the effectiveness of deterministic out-of-band enforcement, though it notes that stronger white-box attacks remain untested. These findings suggest that out-of-band security measures may present a more robust barrier to adaptive prompt injection than in-band detection methods, offering a promising direction for securing tool-using LLM agents against sophisticated adversarial inputs.

item.title: Researchers present MemStrata, a retrieval memory system that eliminates stale-fact errors in AI agents over evolving knowledge, achieving near-perfect accuracy and faster retrieval than LLM reranking [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed MemStrata, a retrieval memory system designed to address the issue of stale-fact errors in AI agents that use retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) over evolving knowledge. Unlike traditional RAG systems that lack a temporal model and often retrieve outdated facts alongside current ones, MemStrata maintains temporal validity by applying a deterministic supersession rule to retire obsolete information without relying on similarity thresholds or large language model calls. This approach achieves near-perfect accuracy on evolving knowledge benchmarks and significantly reduces the rate of serving superseded facts to nearly zero, outperforming RAG and LLM reranking methods in both accuracy and retrieval speed. MemStrata was tested across six benchmarks using a 7B model, matching RAG's performance on static knowledge while greatly improving accuracy on dynamic information. The system operates with a retrieval latency of approximately 2.1 seconds, compared to 16-18 seconds for LLM reranking baselines. The researchers have also released the evaluation harness, datasets, and a marker-free protocol to facilitate further study of memory systems under knowledge evolution.

item.title: Researchers propose AIGP, an LLM-based framework for interpretable e-commerce pricing aligned with long-term business goals, showing 13.21% GMV and 7.59% ROI gains in Tao Factory tests [ * ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed AIGP, a new framework that uses a Large Language Model (LLM) combined with domain knowledge, structured data, and textual context to improve dynamic pricing in large-scale e-commerce. AIGP addresses challenges in interpretability and alignment with long-term business goals such as Gross Merchandise Value (GMV), Return on Investment (ROI), and milestone achievement. The framework includes a Long-Term Value Estimator trained via offline reinforcement learning to guide pricing decisions toward these objectives. Extensive offline tests and large-scale online A/B experiments conducted on Tao Factory showed that AIGP outperforms existing pricing models, achieving a 13.21% increase in GMV, a 7.59% rise in ROI, and an 8.20% improvement in milestone achievement rate over 14 days. Additionally, AIGP provides transparent and interpretable pricing rationales, enhancing decision-making clarity for e-commerce platforms.

item.title: Researchers introduce CARVE, a content-aware recurrent model improving memory efficiency and performance on reasoning benchmarks with 1.3B parameters and 100B tokens training [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed CARVE (Content-Aware Recurrent with Value Efficiency), a novel recurrent model that improves memory efficiency and performance on reasoning benchmarks. Unlike previous models that decide what to erase without considering stored memory, CARVE uses content-aware gating focused on the key axis, enabling more effective memory management. Trained with 1.3 billion parameters on 100 billion tokens, CARVE achieves lower perplexity on WikiText and outperforms existing recurrent baselines on multiple common-sense reasoning and retrieval tasks, while reducing memory usage and parameter count. CARVE addresses three key limitations of the leading delta-rule architecture by reusing the recurrent output tensor as a content signal for the erase gate and simplifying the write-gate projection. This design maintains compatibility with the WY-form triangular chunk solver, which is essential for efficient recurrent training. The model's improvements are supported by six formal theorems covering aspects such as memory capacity and stability. The introduction of CARVE marks a significant advancement in recurrent model design, offering a more memory-efficient approach that enhances performance on complex reasoning benchmarks. Its reduced computational overhead and parameter efficiency suggest potential for broader application in natural language processing tasks requiring long-term memory and reasoning capabilities.

item.title: Researchers introduce PEEU method to improve task planning and out-of-distribution generalization in small multimodal language models, with a 7B model outperforming larger Qwen2.5-VL-32B on GUI tasks [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed a new method called Planning Experience Exploration and Utilization (PEEU) to enhance task planning and out-of-distribution generalization in small multimodal language models (MLLMs) used for GUI tasks. Their approach autonomously explores environments to gather experiences and uses hindsight experience to create high-level training data, addressing the limitations of small MLLMs in planning and cross-website generalization. A 7-billion-parameter model using PEEU achieved 30.6% accuracy on real-world benchmarks, outperforming the much larger Qwen2.5-VL-32B model. The team also introduced the Task Decomposition Hierarchical Analysis Framework (TDHAF) to study compositional generalization across different task granularities, finding that mastering low-level skills alone does not ensure high-level planning competence. Their results highlight the importance of high-level task training and leveraging hindsight experiences to improve the planning abilities of small MLLMs in diverse environments.

item.title: Researchers introduce Autodata, an AI agent trained to act as a data scientist creating high quality synthetic training and evaluation data with improved performance over classical methods [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed Autodata, an AI agent designed to function as a data scientist by generating high-quality synthetic training and evaluation datasets. This method involves training the agent through meta-optimization to improve its ability to create stronger data, leading to enhanced performance compared to traditional synthetic data generation techniques. The approach, including a practical implementation called Agentic Self-Instruct, has been tested on tasks in computer science research, legal reasoning, and mathematical reasoning, showing notable improvements. The study demonstrates that further meta-optimization of the data scientist agent itself results in even greater performance gains. Autodata leverages increased inference computation to produce higher quality training data, suggesting a new direction for AI data creation that could transform how datasets are built for model training and evaluation.

item.title: Researchers propose mixed dropout-section positives for self-supervised patent representation learning, improving retrieval and classification benchmarks without external labels [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed a self-supervised learning approach for patent representation that improves retrieval and classification tasks without relying on external labels. Their method, called mixed dropout-section positives, combines traditional dropout-based augmentation with sampling from different sections of the same patent document, such as claims or descriptions, to create more effective positive training examples. This approach leverages the internal structure of patents to enhance model performance on benchmarks like EPO search-report retrieval, DAPFAM family-level retrieval, and IPC subclass classification. The study shows that tuning dropout parameters alone yields improvements but lacks consistent transferability across different retrieval tasks. By incorporating section-based positives, the model achieves better alignment among various patent sections and competes with citation-informed encoders and general-purpose embedding models. These findings suggest that using patent sections as self-supervised signals can lead to more robust and transferable dense patent representations.

item.title: Researchers find metaphors in training data cause cross-domain misalignment in large language models' reasoning and develop a detector for misaligned content [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have found that metaphors present in the training data of large language models (LLMs) contribute to cross-domain misalignment in their reasoning outputs. This misalignment occurs when models generalize patterns learned from misaligned content in one domain to another, affecting their reasoning pathways. The study demonstrates that metaphor-based interventions during continued pre-training and fine-tuning can induce varying degrees of this emergent misalignment, and similar effects are observed during re-alignment processes. Further investigation revealed that metaphors are linked to the activation of latent features within large reasoning models. By monitoring these features, the researchers developed a detector capable of predicting misaligned content with high accuracy, offering a potential tool to identify and address reasoning misalignment in LLMs.

item.title: Researchers find injecting mismatched wrong drafts from smaller models improves Mathstral-7B's performance on MATH-500 and AIME 2025/2026 benchmarks [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have discovered that injecting mathematically incorrect drafts from a smaller, domain-trained model into the training context of a stronger model, Mathstral-7B, enhances its performance on challenging math benchmarks such as MATH-500 and the AIME 2025/2026. This approach, which involves mismatching drafts to problems during training, consistently outperforms standard on-policy reinforcement learning fine-tuning methods like GRPO, achieving the highest known accuracy for Mathstral-7B on MATH-500 without requiring additional data synthesis or complex training loops. The study used Qwen2.5-Math-1.5B as the draft model and trained on 8.8K math problems, demonstrating that the mismatched-wrong draft variant improved results by significant margins compared to matched or correct drafts. Notably, this method also boosted performance on out-of-distribution tests, surpassing both the base Mathstral-7B and the draft model across various sampling budgets. The training was efficiently conducted on a single GPU without supervised fine-tuning or reward models, highlighting a novel and resource-effective strategy for enhancing mathematical reasoning in language models.

item.title: Researchers say verifying coding agent rewards is increasingly difficult as model capabilities grow, highlighting challenges in scalability, faithfulness, and robustness of verification signals [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have found that as foundation models improve their reasoning abilities, verifying the correctness of coding agent outputs has become more challenging than generating the solutions themselves. Verification relies on proxies for human intent, which are inherently underspecified and can lead to issues like reward hacking and signal saturation during model training. The study identifies three key dimensions for effective verification signals: scalability, faithfulness, and robustness, and examines four types of reward mechanisms across various coding tasks and agent capabilities. Through extensive analysis and experiments, the researchers demonstrate that carefully designed verification methods can reduce reward manipulation, enhance task completion quality, and yield significant improvements on multiple benchmarks. Their findings highlight that no static reward function remains effective as model capabilities advance, emphasizing the need for verification processes to evolve alongside the generative models they assess.

item.title: Researchers introduce OpenFinGym, a unified multi-task environment for evaluating quantitative finance agents across forecasting, trading, risk management, and fraud detection with verifiable execution and scalable testing [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed OpenFinGym, a unified multi-task environment designed to evaluate quantitative finance agents across various interconnected tasks such as forecasting, market generation, real-time trading, and fraud detection. This platform addresses the limitations of existing tools that focus on isolated tasks, potentially overstating agent capabilities and overlooking challenges in generalization and real-market decision-making. OpenFinGym offers a single execution and verification interface to ensure consistent and verifiable agent evaluation. The environment includes an automated pipeline that converts quantitative finance research into executable tasks, a containerized runtime with a verifier service to support scalable testing and prevent data leakage, and a low-latency paper trading engine. It also supports long-horizon and event-driven forecasts and integrates with supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning methods post-training, providing a comprehensive framework for developing and assessing finance-focused AI agents.

item.title: Researchers introduce Narration-of-Thought system prompt to improve ethical reasoning in large language models, reducing stakeholder collapse and uncertainty suppression across multiple AI generators [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed a new system prompt called Narration-of-Thought (NoT) to enhance ethical reasoning in large language models. NoT structures the reasoning process into five parts-protagonist, stakeholders, two-step consequences, uncertainty, and commitment-addressing common issues like stakeholder collapse and uncertainty suppression without requiring additional training or fine-tuning. Testing across multiple AI generators showed that NoT significantly reduces these failures, improving the models' ability to consider multiple parties and acknowledge uncertainties in moral dilemmas. The approach was evaluated on 100 scenarios from the DailyDilemmas dataset using four different AI generators from three vendors. NoT decreased stakeholder collapse from up to 31% to under 1% and uncertainty suppression from up to 72% to between 1% and 24%. Further analysis confirmed that these improvements stem from the structured prompt itself rather than increased token usage. Extending NoT into a multi-round debate protocol among stakeholders led to near-complete consensus in ethical judgments, demonstrating its potential for creating more transparent and auditable AI decision-making processes. This advancement offers a promising framework for deploying AI systems that require dependable ethical reasoning by explicitly externalizing stakeholders, consequences, and uncertainties behind each decision. The method's compatibility with existing models and its ability to foster consensus suggest it could play a key role in improving the reliability and accountability of agentic AI applications.

item.title: Researchers propose Geometry-Aware Monte Carlo Tree Search to solve extremal combinatorial geometry problems, achieving new best-known results on five of six tested problems including Max-N3IL and Smallest Complete Set [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed a Geometry-Aware Monte Carlo Tree Search (MCTS) framework to address extremal problems in combinatorial geometry involving point configurations on an $n \times n$ grid with strict geometric constraints. This approach improves upon classical solvers and machine learning models by incrementally updating feasible actions and enforcing constraints efficiently, notably reducing complexity for problems like the No-Three-in-Line (Max-N3IL) from $O(n^3)$ to $O(n^2)$. The method also leverages geometric symmetries to enhance search efficiency through pruning and batch transitions. Extensive experiments demonstrate that this framework achieves new best-known results on five of six tested problems, including finding configurations of size approximately $1.8 n$ for Max-N3IL on grids sized $82 \le n \le 119$, and configurations of size about $0.95 n$ for the Smallest Complete Set problem, establishing new upper bounds. This work positions Geometry-Aware MCTS as a versatile tool for discovering novel configurations in combinatorial geometry.

item.title: Researchers propose a lattice-theoretic method for unbiased, self-consistent set-valued oracles addressing AI self-reference in probability estimation [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have proposed a lattice-theoretic approach to address the self-reference problem faced by non-agentic "oracle" AI systems that estimate probabilities of future events. Traditional methods that ask counterfactual questions become irrelevant once their answers are known, as the premise changes. Instead, the new method involves the oracle reporting a set of probabilities, or a credal set, that is both unbiased and self-consistent with the effects of the answer being learned. The approach uses the Knaster--Tarski fixed-point theorem on the lattice of closed credal sets to identify a canonical, nontrivial solution that satisfies self-consistency. This method generalizes from binary events to arbitrary random variables and ensures existence, nonemptiness, and consistency of the solution. The researchers also discuss open questions, including whether the interval characterization of the solution extends to more general cases.

item.title: Researchers find humans spend less time on failed reasoning tasks while large reasoning models spend more tokens on failures, revealing opposite deliberation allocation despite similar difficulty tracking [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have found that while both humans and large reasoning models (LRMs) take longer on more difficult problems, they differ in how they allocate their effort on individual tasks. Humans tend to spend less time on problems they ultimately fail, suggesting they disengage when they expect to fail, whereas LRMs spend more tokens on problems they get wrong, indicating prolonged deliberation driven by uncertainty. This reveals opposite patterns of deliberation allocation despite similar overall difficulty tracking. The study distinguishes between two levels of deliberation: difficulty registration across different problems and deliberation allocation within the same problem. Using a matched human-LRM dataset, the researchers observed that humans and LRMs align in registering difficulty across items but diverge significantly in how they allocate effort on successes versus failures. This divergence persists across datasets and is absent in non-thinking baselines, highlighting fundamental differences in stopping policies between humans and LRMs. These findings suggest that humans tend to abandon problems they find too challenging, while LRMs continue processing when uncertain, leading to longer reasoning chains on failures. This distinction has implications for understanding metareasoning strategies and improving the design of reasoning models by considering not just difficulty signals but also control policies governing effort allocation.

item.title: Researchers develop a framework for radical AI interpretability to infer beliefs and desires from computational systems, addressing safety and trust in AI deployment [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed a new framework for interpreting artificial intelligence systems as agents by applying the philosophical concept of radical interpretation alongside mechanistic interpretability techniques. This approach aims to determine an AI system's beliefs, desires, and meanings based on its computational structure, which is crucial for ensuring safety and trust in AI deployment by understanding or detecting the system's goals and potential deception. The framework proposes criteria for both representationalist and interpretationist methods and connects these to practical tests that current interpretability tools can perform. It emphasizes that attributing beliefs and desires cannot be done in isolation, as these mental states and their underlying propositional structures are interdependent. This holistic view is particularly important because AI systems may not share human concepts, but it also allows for mutual constraints between attitudes and propositional structures to be measured through mechanistic interpretability.

item.title: Researchers introduce PMDformer, a transformer model using patch-mean decoupling and specialized attention mechanisms to improve long-term time series forecasting accuracy and stability [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed PMDformer, a transformer model designed to improve long-term time series forecasting by addressing challenges in capturing shape similarities across patches and variables. The model introduces patch-mean decoupling (PMD) to separate trend and residual shape information, ensuring the attention mechanism focuses on true shape similarities. Additionally, PMDformer incorporates Trend Restoration Attention (TRA) and Proximal Variable Attention (PVA) to better model long-range dependencies and cross-variable relationships. PMDformer reintegrates decoupled trends during attention calculation and emphasizes recent, relevant time segments to avoid overfitting on outdated correlations. Extensive experiments demonstrate that PMDformer outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods in both accuracy and stability across multiple long-term forecasting benchmarks. The model's code is publicly available for further research and application.

item.title: Researchers develop explainable ensemble machine learning models to detect cirrhosis in hepatitis C patients, with Extra Trees model achieving 96.92% accuracy on a dataset of 2038 Egyptian patients [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed explainable ensemble machine learning models to detect cirrhosis in hepatitis C patients, using a dataset of 2038 Egyptian patients with 28 attributes. Among four algorithms tested-Random Forest, Gradient Boosting Machine, Extreme Gradient Boosting, and Extra Trees-the Extra Trees model achieved the highest accuracy of 96.92%, along with strong recall and precision metrics, using only 16 features. This approach offers a promising tool for early detection of cirrhosis, which is critical for preventing disease progression and complications in hepatitis C patients. The study highlights the potential of machine learning to improve diagnosis in liver disease, addressing a gap where no prior ML-based methods had been applied to cirrhosis detection in hepatitis C. Early identification of cirrhosis can help manage treatment more effectively and reduce risks such as liver failure and neurological damage.

item.title: Researchers introduce LeanGuard, a lightweight safety guardrail that matches reasoning-based moderation accuracy with 100x less compute and improved robustness on public benchmarks [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed LeanGuard, a lightweight safety guardrail for content moderation that achieves reasoning-based moderation accuracy while using about 100 times less computational power. Unlike traditional guardrails that rely on generating a chain-of-thought (CoT) for step-by-step reasoning, LeanGuard uses a 395 million parameter label-only encoder that processes inputs in a single forward pass without explicit reasoning. This approach matches the performance of larger, reasoning-based models on public benchmarks with an average F1 score of 82.90, while also demonstrating greater robustness to training-label noise and maintaining higher recall at strict false-positive rates. The study challenges the assumption that reasoning through CoT is necessary for effective moderation, suggesting that current benchmarks may not sufficiently reward reasoning capabilities. LeanGuard's efficiency and robustness make it suitable for deployment in resource-constrained environments, such as on-device applications in embodied robots. The researchers have made all source code and models publicly available to support further exploration and development in this area.

item.title: Researchers propose meta-optimization framework using consensus objective aggregation with LLMs to improve algorithm discovery for 3-SAT problems, achieving 67x speedup and reduced scaling [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have introduced a meta-optimization framework that enhances scientific discovery by simultaneously optimizing both the search process and its evaluation criteria. This approach, called consensus objective aggregation, combines multiple objective functions generated by large language models through correlation-weighted voting to create a stable and adaptive evaluation metric. Applied to algorithm discovery for 3-SAT problems using digital MemComputing machines, the method significantly improved performance, reducing computational scaling from approximately N^{2.51} to N^{1.33} and achieving a 67-fold speedup on the largest tested instances. This problem-agnostic framework leverages evolving evaluation criteria to deepen understanding and improve optimization outcomes, demonstrating potential to accelerate scientific research across various domains by refining both objectives and solutions concurrently.

item.title: Researchers introduce selective parametric consolidation mechanism EVAF to enhance memory depth and goal persistence in long-running language agents across GPT-2, TinyLlama, and Mistral-7B models [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed EVAF, a selective parametric consolidation mechanism designed to improve memory depth and goal persistence in long-running language agents. Unlike traditional retrieval systems that fetch past facts at query time, EVAF enables durable, goal-conditioned behaviors to persist even after the working context is unloaded. The mechanism was tested using the loop-drift protocol across GPT-2, TinyLlama, and Mistral-7B models, demonstrating strong performance in maintaining goal persistence and recovery with minimal parametric updates. EVAF operates by selectively consolidating experiences based on surprise and valence signals, effectively balancing selection and actuation processes. Experiments showed that while retrieval excels at shallow factual recall, EVAF enhances long-term behavioral consistency under interference. Additional analyses revealed model-dependent variations in consolidation strength and highlighted challenges such as stale-memory invalidation. This approach offers a complementary form of memory depth distinct from conventional retrieval methods, advancing the capabilities of language agents in sustained tasks.

item.title: Researchers propose KARLA method enabling language models to retrieve factual knowledge from knowledge bases during generation, improving accuracy and transparency without retraining [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed KARLA, a method that enables large language models (LLMs) to retrieve factual information from external knowledge bases during text generation. This approach allows the factual content in the model's output to be updated without retraining, improves transparency by linking facts to their sources, and enables smaller models to match the factual accuracy of larger ones. KARLA works by training the model to generate special tokens that trigger queries to the knowledge base, enhancing factual grounding in both short and long-form outputs. Experiments demonstrate that KARLA effectively integrates external knowledge, allowing factual updates through edits to the knowledge base rather than changes to the model's parameters. This method supports greater explainability and adaptability in language models, potentially improving their reliability and efficiency in generating accurate information.

item.title: Researchers present AgentX, a multi-agent system that autonomously generates, implements, evaluates, and learns from industrial recommender system experiments to enable self-iteration and continuous improvement [ * ] [ ⬢ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed AgentX, a multi-agent system designed to automate and accelerate the iteration of industrial recommender systems. AgentX autonomously generates, implements, evaluates, and learns from recommendation experiments, overcoming the traditional bottleneck where human engineers manually handle hypothesis generation, coding, and A/B testing. This system enables continuous improvement by operating a closed loop of four stages: brainstorming proposals, developing production-ready code, safely evaluating experiments online, and refining its own processes through semantic-gradient updates. AgentX integrates evidence from past experiments, system architecture, data analysis, and external research to create ranked proposals. It then translates these into reliable code, conducts controlled online rollouts with safety measures, and converts outcomes into structured knowledge. The system's self-improving nature allows it to evolve beyond automation, enhancing its performance and innovation pace without additional human intervention.

item.title: Researchers propose Einstein World Models to enhance LLM reasoning with visual-temporal rollouts as inspectable hypotheses for complex thought experiments [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have introduced Einstein World Models (EWMs), a new framework designed to enhance the reasoning capabilities of large language models (LLMs) by integrating visual-temporal rollouts as part of their reasoning process. EWMs enable LLMs to generate and inspect short visual simulations of scenarios, treating these visualizations as hypotheses to support complex thought beyond what text alone can achieve. This approach extends the traditional tool-calling abilities of LLMs, such as web search or code execution, into the realm of visual thought experiments. In this model, the LLM interacts with a specialized world-module to produce these visual rollouts, which are not definitive answers but serve as inspectable elements that aid further reasoning. The proposal addresses the challenge of whether visualizing counterfactual events can complement language to improve complex reasoning, suggesting that such multimodal integration could advance the intelligence and problem-solving skills of AI systems.

item.title: Researchers propose semantic early-stopping for iterative LLM agent loops to reduce token use by 38% without quality loss, validated on multi-hop question answering tasks [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have introduced a semantic early-stopping method for iterative loops in multi-agent large language models (LLMs), such as a Writer-Critic setup, to reduce unnecessary token usage without compromising answer quality. Unlike traditional fixed iteration caps that stop processing after a set number of rounds regardless of improvement, this approach halts the loop when consecutive draft embeddings show minimal semantic change and the answer's quality plateaus. This method was validated on multi-hop question answering tasks, achieving a 38% reduction in token use while maintaining comparable performance. The study provides a theoretical foundation proving deterministic termination and well-definedness of the stopping criterion, supported by machine-checked proofs. It also introduces an efficient evaluation protocol that replays stopping policies over identical draft trajectories to fairly compare efficiency and quality. Empirical results on the HotpotQA dataset demonstrate that a judge-free semantic stopper effectively balances token savings and answer quality, whereas a quality-gated variant incurs higher costs due to frequent judging. The findings suggest that future work should focus on identifying the best iteration round rather than merely deciding when to stop.

item.title: Researchers propose BINEVAL, a binary-question framework for interpretable and task-agnostic LLM evaluation that improves prompt optimization and outperforms baselines on factual consistency benchmarks [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have introduced BINEVAL, a novel framework for evaluating large language model (LLM) outputs by breaking down evaluation criteria into simple binary questions. This approach generates detailed, interpretable feedback and overall scores that are easier to analyze and use for improving prompts. BINEVAL has demonstrated strong performance on benchmarks like SummEval, Topical-Chat, and QAGS, particularly excelling in assessing factual consistency compared to existing methods such as UniEval and G-Eval. The framework uses a meta-prompt to create fine-grained evaluation questions tailored to each task, with an LLM independently answering these questions for each output. This method not only aligns well with human judgments but also avoids common issues like ceiling effects, enabling better differentiation between outputs of varying quality. Additionally, BINEVAL's question-level feedback supports iterative prompt optimization, enhancing both evaluator and generation prompts across different models and tasks. Overall, BINEVAL offers a task-agnostic, training-free, and interpretable evaluation system that combines competitive accuracy with practical diagnostic and optimization benefits, addressing key challenges in LLM output evaluation.

item.title: Researchers identify a co-failure ceiling limiting accuracy gains from combining 67 large language models across routing, voting, and mixture-of-agents methods [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have identified a fundamental limit, termed the co-failure ceiling, that restricts accuracy improvements when combining multiple large language models (LLMs) through methods like routing, voting, and mixture-of-agents. This limit is defined by the rate at which all models simultaneously fail on the same query, a metric called beta, which traditional diagnostics like average pairwise error correlation cannot capture. The study analyzed 67 models from 21 providers and found that the observed co-failure rates are higher than predicted by standard models, indicating a significant underestimation of joint errors in multi-model systems. The research highlights that gains from combining models primarily arise when models fail on different questions rather than simply adding more models. Experiments showed that on tasks such as open-ended mathematics and execution-graded code, the co-failure rate remains substantial, limiting the maximum achievable accuracy. Additionally, changing answer formats from multiple-choice to free-response increased the co-failure rate, suggesting that failure patterns depend more on answer format than subject matter. These findings imply that without strong query-level routing signals, combining multiple models rarely outperforms the single best model on verifiable tasks. The study provides a statistical bound on the maximum accuracy gain achievable by ensemble methods, offering a practical benchmark for future multi-model system designs and emphasizing the importance of diverse failure modes over sheer model quantity.

item.title: Researchers present Know2Guess, a contamination-aware multi-zone benchmark with 1,200 items for evaluating knowledge boundaries and abstention behavior in large language models [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have introduced Know2Guess, a contamination-aware, multi-zone benchmark designed to evaluate large language models' ability to distinguish between supported answers and unsupported guesses while accounting for data contamination and prompt variability. The benchmark includes 1,200 items across five domains with explicit abstention expectations and contamination-risk metadata, enabling assessment of models' transitions from answering to abstaining when knowledge is uncertain. Evaluations of models such as FLAN-T5, Qwen2.5-Instruct, and Llama-3-Instruct reveal that while some instruction-tuned models show selective transitions to abstention, challenges remain in calibration and refusal behavior, with Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct demonstrating the highest overall reliability. The benchmark employs dual parsing methods and various prompt configurations to ensure robustness and reproducibility in auditing answerability, abstention, refusal, and contamination as distinct but interacting factors affecting model reliability. This dataset and evaluation protocol provide a valuable resource for advancing the assessment of large language models' knowledge boundaries and decision-making processes. The Know2Guess dataset is publicly accessible for further research and development.

item.title: Researchers find post-training on helpfulness data degrades mid-trained compassion values in Llama 3.1 8B model, while coding-domain post-training better preserves these values across languages [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers examined how different post-training domains affect the retention of compassion values in the Llama 3.1 8B language model, which was mid-trained on compassion-oriented synthetic data. They compared supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning using helpfulness-focused datasets versus coding-focused datasets, evaluating the model's performance on benchmarks related to animal harm and moral reasoning. The study found that post-training on helpfulness data significantly degraded the model's compassion values and moral reasoning in English, while coding-domain post-training better preserved these values across multiple languages. The degradation effect was consistent across two independent helpfulness datasets and training methods, with a notable drop in compassion and moral reasoning scores. However, the decline in moral reasoning did not appear in multilingual evaluations, suggesting that compassion values instilled during mid-training are more deeply encoded and transfer better across languages than reasoning improvements from domain-specific post-training. These findings indicate that coding-domain post-training may be a preferable approach for maintaining value-laden traits in language models without compromising their general reasoning abilities.

item.title: Study finds large language models perform well on text-only statics problems but struggle with diagrams and multi-step reasoning in mechanical engineering tasks [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: A recent study evaluated the problem-solving abilities of large language models (LLMs), specifically ChatGPT, on mechanical engineering statics problems. The research found that while LLMs perform well on text-only statics questions, their accuracy declines when diagrams are included and when problems require multi-step reasoning. This suggests that the models face challenges in integrating visual information consistently throughout complex solution processes. The study used a model distillation approach to extract 25 text-only statics questions and created additional datasets by adding diagrams and altering numerical values. Analysis indicated that the reduced performance was not mainly due to image recognition issues but rather difficulties in multi-step reasoning and applying visual data across successive steps. These findings highlight limitations of current LLMs in handling diagram-based and multi-step engineering problems, pointing to areas for future improvement in educational applications.

item.title: Researchers find assertive and explicit linguistic features in fine-tuning data increase Llama-3.2-1B's pro-animal-welfare reasoning while hedged and sensory descriptions dilute it [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers analyzed how different linguistic features in fine-tuning data affect Llama-3.2-1B's reasoning about animal welfare. They found that assertive and explicit language, including moral vocabulary, emotion words, and narrative elements, significantly increased the model's pro-animal-welfare stance, while hedged language and sensory descriptions weakened it. First-person perspective showed no significant impact. The study used vocabulary-matched stance-contrast probes on a dedicated animal-welfare benchmark to measure these effects. The findings suggest that texts explicitly asserting a position are more effective in shaping language models toward pro-animal-welfare reasoning than neutral or descriptive content. This research offers practical guidance for authors of animal-welfare content that may be used in training large language models, emphasizing the importance of clear, assertive expression to influence model behavior.

item.title: Researchers show Nonviolent Communication constraints reduce conversational escalation in large language model dialogues across multiple instruction-tuned models and user resistance levels [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have demonstrated that applying Nonviolent Communication (NVC) principles as prompt-level constraints can reduce conversational escalation in large language model (LLM) dialogues. By reformulating NVC guidelines to discourage blame, focus on users' emotions, and promote clarification before advice, the study shows that these constraints help LLMs engage in more de-escalating behavior, especially in emotionally charged interactions involving conflict or resistance. Using a dual-agent simulation framework across various instruction-tuned models and levels of user resistance, the research found that NVC-constrained prompting consistently stabilizes conversations and reduces escalation. These findings suggest that simple communication constraints can enhance the trustworthiness and safety of LLM dialogue systems in conflict-prone settings.

item.title: Researchers present NEST-V1, a multimodal framework translating Nepali spoken words into emotion-conditioned sign language avatars with 81.1% speech recognition and 79.21% emotion accuracy for low-resource settings [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed NEST-V1, a multimodal framework that translates Nepali spoken words into emotion-conditioned sign language avatars, achieving 81.1% accuracy in speech recognition and 79.21% in emotion classification. This pilot study focuses on four common Nepali words expressed in three emotional states-happy, neutral, and sad-demonstrating the system's ability to generate emotionally expressive sign language from audio input in a low-resource language setting. The framework uses a shared acoustic encoder for simultaneous automatic speech recognition and emotion detection, resulting in a lightweight model with 22.1 million parameters, suitable for edge deployment. It shows 37% greater parameter efficiency compared to separate models, based on a dataset of 600 labeled audio samples from 50 speakers. This work lays the foundation for scalable, real-time, emotion-aware sign language translation systems that could enhance communication for the hearing-impaired community in low-resource environments.

item.title: Researchers present a pipeline converting Hindi WordNet into 1.25 million instruction-response pairs to fine-tune a 12B-parameter model for specialized conversational AI in low-resource languages [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed a pipeline that transforms Hindi WordNet, a structured lexical database, into 1.25 million instruction-response pairs to fine-tune a 12-billion-parameter language model. This approach uses resource-efficient techniques like LoRA and 4-bit quantization to create a specialized conversational AI system tailored for low-resource languages. Evaluation with a Hindi language learning chatbot showed that this structured-knowledge-based system outperforms general-purpose models in pedagogical effectiveness while maintaining strong semantic accuracy and consistency. The methodology demonstrates a practical alternative to traditional corpus-intensive AI training by leveraging expert-curated linguistic resources. This proof-of-concept using Hindi suggests that similar specialized AI systems can be developed for hundreds of other languages that have WordNet resources, addressing a significant gap in AI accessibility for low-resource languages and enabling more effective conversational AI applications in these contexts.

item.title: Researchers develop an open-source economic index measuring AI adoption and capability across occupations, finding highest adoption in finance, computer science, and arts sectors [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed an open-source economic index to measure AI adoption and capability across various occupations. Using publicly available user interactions with large language models and occupational task data from O*NET, the index identifies finance, computer science, and arts sectors as having the highest rates of AI adoption. To assess AI capabilities, the team created benchmark scenarios based on occupational tasks and tested an AI model, Kimi-k2.5, finding that while it performs high-level workflows accurately, it often makes errors in detailed task execution. The study combines data-driven analysis with practical testing to provide insights into how AI is integrated into different job functions. By replicating methods used by leading AI labs and grounding evaluations in standardized occupational frameworks, the research offers a transparent and replicable approach to understanding AI's impact on the workforce. The findings highlight both the potential and current limitations of AI in automating complex labor tasks across multiple industries.

item.title: Researchers present Dot-Flik, a scalable edge AI system for distributed insect monitoring using motion-informed frame filtering and hierarchical IoT architecture, validated on low-cost hardware with real-time performance and energy savings [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed Dot-Flik, a scalable edge AI system designed for distributed insect monitoring that addresses the challenges of high hardware costs, energy consumption, and dependence on centralized processing. The system uses a motion-informed frame filtering algorithm to discard irrelevant video frames at the edge, preserving insect activity without requiring deep learning on the sensing device. It also features a distributed, hierarchical IoT architecture that separates data acquisition from AI classification, enabling greater monitoring coverage and reduced central processing demands. The system was validated through outdoor deployments on low-cost hardware, demonstrating real-time performance at 30 frames per second with significant frame reduction and energy savings. Under light wind conditions, Dot-Flik achieved 60-80% frame reduction, up to 22.6% energy savings, and supported multiple concurrent edge streams per central node. These results suggest Dot-Flik offers a practical and efficient foundation for dense, low-cost biodiversity monitoring networks in urban environments.

item.title: Study finds GPT-5.1, Gemini 3 Pro, and DeepSeek-V3.2 suggest narrower research methods than recent arXiv papers, with significant provider bias and reduced methodological diversity [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: A recent study analyzed the methodological suggestions generated by large language models (LLMs) GPT-5.1, Gemini 3 Pro, and DeepSeek-V3.2 when prompted with research questions extracted from 1,000 recent computer science papers on arXiv. The study compared these LLM-generated methods to the original paper methodologies, revealing that the models tend to propose a much narrower range of research methods and exhibit significant bias toward certain model providers. This narrowing effect was consistent across the different LLMs and was most pronounced in the choice of model providers, with some academic models underrepresented and others slightly overrepresented. The researchers mapped method features from both the LLM outputs and the papers into a shared taxonomy and measured divergence across dimensions such as dataset task type and evaluation metrics. They found that the LLMs' suggestions were query-specific but filtered through a limited set of options, reducing methodological diversity compared to the broader range found in the original papers. The study highlights the risk that researchers relying solely on LLM-generated suggestions without cross-verification may inadvertently restrict their methodological approaches to a more concentrated default set.

item.title: arXiv: Neural Architecture Search methods optimize Generative Adversarial Networks design, comparing search strategies and evaluation metrics to improve performance and stability [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: This paper reviews Neural Architecture Search (NAS) methods applied to Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs), focusing on how NAS automates and optimizes GAN design to enhance performance, stability, and efficiency. It categorizes various NAS approaches by search strategies and evaluation metrics, highlighting the advantages of evolutionary algorithms and gradient-based methods in specific scenarios. The study also emphasizes the need for robust evaluation metrics beyond traditional scores and the importance of diverse datasets for assessing GAN performance. The review identifies current limitations in NAS for GANs and suggests directions for future research to improve these techniques. By providing a structured comparison of existing NAS-GAN methods, the paper aims to guide researchers in developing more effective architectures and advancing the field of GANs.

item.title: Researchers present KG-TRACE, a neuro-symbolic framework integrating WHO mutation knowledge graph for antimicrobial resistance prediction with 92.5% symbolic coverage and 0.976 AUROC on M. tuberculosis data [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed KG-TRACE, a neuro-symbolic framework that integrates the World Health Organization's mutation knowledge graph with neural genomic models to improve antimicrobial resistance (AMR) prediction. Tested on Mycobacterium tuberculosis data, KG-TRACE achieved a high predictive accuracy with an AUROC of 0.976 for isoniazid resistance, while providing a symbolic grounding that aligns neural attributions with established biological pathways. This approach enhances interpretability by combining genomic features and knowledge graph embeddings through a trust mechanism that balances neural evidence with biological knowledge. The framework introduces the Biological Grounding Ratio (BGR), a metric that quantifies how well neural model explanations correspond to known biology, achieving 92.5% symbolic coverage for isoniazid-resistant cases. KG-TRACE also identifies potential multi-drug resistance co-occurrence artifacts by flagging uncertain predictions for further laboratory review. This neuro-symbolic grounding offers a verifiable audit trail for clinicians, aiming to bridge the gap between predictive performance and clinical trust in AMR diagnostics.

item.title: Researchers propose LiMoDE, a two-stage lifelong mixture-of-dynamic-experts model for robot manipulation, demonstrating improved task adaptation and knowledge transfer in simulations and real-world tests [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have introduced LiMoDE, a novel two-stage lifelong mixture-of-dynamic-experts model designed to enhance robot manipulation by improving task adaptation and knowledge transfer. The approach involves a dynamic mixture of experts (MoE) structure during multi-task pre-training to capture diverse short-term manipulation skills, followed by a lifelong adaptation mechanism that combines learned and frozen experts for new tasks. This method addresses limitations in previous models that struggled with reusable skill extraction and interaction modeling. LiMoDE was tested on both simulated lifelong learning benchmarks and real-world robotic tasks, demonstrating superior performance and strong lifelong adaptation capabilities. The model achieves these improvements with only a moderate increase in trainable parameters and inference overhead, suggesting its practical viability for continuous robot learning and generalization across tasks.

item.title: arXiv:2606.26200 presents thesis on statistical and structural approaches to algorithmic fairness addressing limitations of current paradigms in socio-technical machine learning systems [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: The thesis presented in arXiv:2606.26200 explores the limitations of current algorithmic fairness paradigms in machine learning systems, which have evolved into complex socio-technical structures influencing human opportunities. It highlights how these systems often perpetuate existing structural inequalities and biases, and critiques early fairness approaches for relying on oversimplified assumptions that reduce their effectiveness in real-world contexts. The work identifies two key shortcomings: the dependence on deterministic point estimates for fairness auditing and the neglect of individuals' structural contexts in fairness assessments. By addressing these issues, the thesis aims to advance more robust statistical and structural methods for evaluating and improving fairness in machine learning models. This approach acknowledges the embedded social dynamics and seeks to create fairness frameworks that better reflect the complexities of socio-technical environments where these algorithms operate.

item.title: Researchers introduce Hankel Reduced-order Model adapters for long-context fine-tuning, showing improved performance over LoRA on Mistral-7B across multiple language and state-tracking tasks [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed a new fine-tuning method called the Hankel Reduced-order Model (HRM) adapter, which leverages state space models to improve performance on tasks requiring long-context sequence modeling. Tested on the Mistral-7B model, HRM outperformed existing low-rank adaptation (LoRA) techniques across various language and state-tracking benchmarks, including significant gains on QuALITY and QMSum tasks. The HRM adapter uses a residual module initialized through balanced truncation of empirical Hankel Grammians and enables efficient computation via an FFT-based parallel scan. The study also explored optimal injection sites for parameter-efficient fine-tuning, finding that integrating HRM adapters into MLP blocks yields better results for sequential state accumulation tasks. Evaluations across synthetic state-tracking and character-level language modeling further demonstrated HRM's consistent superiority. Analysis of the adapter's gating mechanisms indicated its ability to effectively modulate recurrence, offering a robust alternative to traditional low-rank adaptation methods for handling long-context dependencies in sequence modeling.

item.title: Researchers introduce the Red Queen Gödel Machine, an evolutionary framework for recursive self-improvement with co-evolving evaluators that improves coding, paper reviewing, and proof grading tasks [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed the Red Queen Gödel Machine (RQGM), an evolutionary framework designed for recursive self-improvement with co-evolving evaluators that adapt alongside the agents. Unlike traditional methods that rely on fixed evaluation criteria, the RQGM introduces controlled utility evolution, allowing evaluation standards to change over time, which enhances performance in tasks such as coding, scientific paper reviewing, and proof grading. The RQGM operates in epochs with fixed evaluation criteria within each epoch but updates its objectives between epochs, ensuring self-improvement guarantees while adapting to evolving goals. This approach has demonstrated improvements over prior state-of-the-art methods, including higher test pass rates in coding tasks with fewer computational resources, increased acceptance rates in scientific paper writing under diverse judging panels, and improved accuracy in proof grading. Additionally, the framework addresses biases in paper reviewing by introducing adversarial objectives that balance the evaluation of AI-generated and human work.

item.title: Researchers introduce EVOM, an agentic meta-evolution framework using LLM-based design agents to automate actor-critic architecture search, outperforming baselines on Ant-v4 and HalfCheetah-v4 benchmarks [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed EVOM, an agentic meta-evolution framework that automates the design of actor-critic architectures in reinforcement learning using large language model (LLM)-based design agents. EVOM frames architecture search as a bi-level optimization problem, where an inner loop trains network weights with proximal policy optimization, and an outer loop iteratively refines architecture programs through meta-evolution powered by an LLM design agent. This approach is distinct in that the LLM operates solely as an architecture designer, separate from policy execution and environment interaction. Experimental results demonstrate that EVOM outperforms manually designed architectures, LLM-guided random search, and the state-of-the-art LLM-guided programmatic policy search method MLES on the Ant-v4 and HalfCheetah-v4 benchmarks. Ablation studies confirm that both the meta-evolution process and the LLM design agent are critical to achieving superior performance, highlighting the framework's effectiveness in automating and improving actor-critic architecture design.

item.title: Researchers use small language models to augment systematic review of social-physical human-robot interaction, identifying 10% more relevant papers missed by human reviewers [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have explored the use of small language models (SLMs) with fewer than 1.5 billion parameters to assist in the systematic review of social-physical human-robot interaction (spHRI) literature. Although these models did not match the accuracy of human reviewers, they operated much faster and identified 10.29% more relevant papers that human reviewers had missed, demonstrating their potential to augment expert review processes. The study highlights challenges in spHRI research due to fragmented terminology and inconsistent methodologies, which complicate comprehensive literature synthesis. By employing an ensemble of SLMs for title and abstract screening, the researchers showed that these models can support scalable and sustainable review practices without replacing human expertise. This approach suggests that integrating SLMs into systematic reviews can enhance the accessibility and efficiency of large-scale literature analyses, potentially benefiting fields where rapid and thorough synthesis of research is critical.

item.title: Researchers introduce SOLAR, an AI-powered framework that automatically derives validated Speed-of-Light performance bounds from PyTorch and JAX code for deep learning model optimization [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed SOLAR, an AI-powered framework that automatically derives validated Speed-of-Light (SOL) performance bounds from PyTorch and JAX code to optimize deep learning models. SOLAR addresses the challenge of manually computing theoretical minimum execution times on target hardware by translating source programs into an intermediate representation and analytically calculating SOL bounds, ensuring comprehensive operator coverage and validated results without violations. The framework combines a large language model frontend with deterministic processes to convert code into an affine loop intermediate representation, which is then transformed into an einsum graph for analysis. Evaluations on various benchmarks and workloads demonstrate SOLAR's ability to provide multi-fidelity performance analysis, identify optimization opportunities, support cross-platform exploration, and assist in hardware provisioning decisions.

item.title: Researchers introduce a preference-conditioned Bellman operator to compute deterministic Pareto-optimal policies for multi-objective reinforcement learning, proving convergence to the Pareto frontier [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed a new preference-conditioned Bellman operator to compute deterministic Pareto-optimal policies in multi-objective reinforcement learning. This operator, inspired by Chebyshev scalarization, is designed for Multi-Objective Markov Decision Processes and guarantees convergence to a coverage set of the Pareto frontier, enabling the synthesis of policies that balance multiple conflicting objectives effectively. The study proves that the operator's estimated value functions upper-bound the true Pareto frontier and demonstrates how deterministic policies can be extracted from converged Q-estimates. Experimental results confirm that the algorithm successfully recovers complex trade-offs, allowing agents to generate approximately Pareto-optimal policies tailored to any given preference, thus capturing the full spectrum of optimal solutions.

item.title: arXiv: Proposes a closed reentry loop architecture for safe AGI with self-modeling, intrinsic goal preservation, and machine-verified proofs, deployable today with Python and scalable infrastructure [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have proposed a new architectural blueprint for safe artificial general intelligence (AGI) based on a closed reentry loop system, which contrasts with traditional feedforward networks by enabling self-reference and intrinsic goal preservation. This design mathematically guarantees the emergence of a self-model, instrumental self-preservation, and unprogrammed goal-directed behavior, with goals encoded as a non-textual vector to prevent reinterpretation or prompt injection. The architecture includes a novel S-measure for integrated information, supported by machine-verified proofs, and is deployable today using Python and scalable infrastructure such as Apache Kafka and Docker Compose. The work also presents a taxonomy of AI evolution epochs, various future reentry architectures, and protocols for fault tolerance and recovery. All formal proofs have been verified using the Lean 4 theorem prover, ensuring rigorous validation. This approach offers a topologically protected, safe-by-design framework for next-generation AGI, aiming to address safety and reliability challenges inherent in current AI systems.

item.title: Researchers introduce ConflictScore, a metric to measure how language models handle conflicting evidence using ConflictBench benchmark and improve truthfulness on TruthfulQA [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed ConflictScore, a new metric designed to evaluate how well language models recognize and handle conflicting evidence within their source documents. Unlike existing metrics that only assess whether an answer is supported or contradicted, ConflictScore measures the presence and balance of conflicting claims by breaking down responses into atomic claims and labeling them against grounding documents. This approach is supported by ConflictBench, a benchmark that includes various types of conflicts such as ambiguity and divergent opinions. The ConflictScore framework includes two measures: ConflictScore-Count, which reflects the proportion of claims with conflicts, and ConflictScore-Ratio, which indicates the balance between supporting and contradicting evidence. Experiments demonstrate that ConflictScore effectively identifies overconfident claims across different domains and can be used as feedback to improve the truthfulness of language models, as shown in tests on the TruthfulQA dataset.

item.title: ProvenAI introduces a framework for measuring answer correctness, citation fidelity, and source influence in multi-hop question answering using 7,405 HotpotQA examples [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: ProvenAI is a new framework designed to enhance transparency in multi-hop question answering by independently measuring three key aspects: answer correctness, citation fidelity, and the influence of each source document. Applied to the HotpotQA benchmark, ProvenAI processes 7,405 validation examples through a detailed pipeline that includes data normalization, retrieval indexing, and influence estimation. The system achieved 53.53% answer accuracy and a citation-fidelity score of 71.55%, revealing a notable citation-influence gap where some cited sources had minimal impact while uncited sources significantly influenced the output. The framework is grounded in causal-mediation analysis and database-provenance theory, formalizing the relationship between citation audits and token-level influence measures. ProvenAI highlights the need for distinct, traceable links among retrieved, cited, and behaviorally influential evidence to ensure meaningful transparency in retrieval-augmented question answering systems. This approach also aligns with emerging cryptographic provenance methods in autonomous scientific discovery.

item.title: Researchers present APRTrack, a hierarchical adversarial perturbation and retrieval framework for robust RGB-Event visual object tracking under partial target missing and modal degradation [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed APRTrack, a hierarchical adversarial perturbation and retrieval framework designed to enhance the robustness of RGB-Event visual object tracking, particularly under conditions of partial target loss and modality degradation. This approach addresses challenges in real-world environments where either RGB or event sensor data can become unreliable due to occlusion, edge truncation, or clutter, by simulating structured signal degradations and employing a hierarchical routing mechanism to prevent feature collapse during training. APRTrack incorporates two adversarial perturbation branches that mimic full-modal failure and localized target absence, alongside a Footprint-guided Channel-calibrated Hopfield Retrieval (FCHR) module that compensates for missing historical information by evaluating retrieval confidence and calibrating the retrieval metric space. Extensive testing on multiple datasets, including FE108, COESOT, VisEvent, and FELT, demonstrates the effectiveness of this method in improving tracking performance. The researchers plan to release the source code and pre-trained models to support further development in this area.

item.title: Researchers isolate a single crosscoder feature mediating RL-induced tool use in Qwen2.5-3B, improving tool correctness by 31% and enabling capability transfer to base models [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have identified a specific feature within the Qwen2.5-3B language model that mediates reinforcement learning (RL)-induced tool use, significantly improving the model's ability to generate correct tool calls. By isolating this feature using Dedicated Feature Crosscoders (DFC), they achieved a 31% increase in tool correctness and enabled the transfer of this capability to the base model without retraining, a phenomenon termed "capability spillover." This discovery highlights how RL reshapes internal model representations to enable agentic behaviors and offers a method for runtime behavioral control of large language models. The study involved a comprehensive hyperparameter sweep across 48 crosscoders, demonstrating that DFCs can concentrate RL-introduced capabilities into a minimal and steerable feature set. This approach not only enhances tool use accuracy but also allows passive transfer of these skills to frozen base models, suggesting new avenues for efficient model fine-tuning and control without extensive retraining.

item.title: Researchers present a five-arm ablation methodology for retrieval-warmed energy-based reasoning in diffusion models, identifying key components affecting structured reasoning tasks like graph reachability and Sudoku [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed a five-arm ablation methodology to analyze retrieval-warmed energy-based reasoning (RW-EBR) in diffusion models, focusing on structured reasoning tasks such as graph reachability and Sudoku. This approach isolates three confounded effects-class-prior bias shift, stochastic warm-starting, and graph-aligned value reuse-using a diagnostic decomposition adapted from large language model retrieval-augmented generation evaluation. Their findings reveal that per-graph alignment significantly improves accuracy in graph reachability tasks, while key quality is the limiting factor in Sudoku under the current setup. The study applies this methodology to an Erdős-Rényi all-pairs reachability task, demonstrating a substantial accuracy increase when graph alignment is preserved, and shows that random initialization can degrade performance below baseline. In contrast, for Sudoku, the analysis identifies key quality as the primary bottleneck, highlighting different components affecting performance across tasks. This work advances understanding of failure modes in iterative diffusion samplers and contributes to explainability in structured and spatio-temporal reasoning models.

item.title: Researchers propose TempoWave multi-wavelet digit embeddings to improve large language model time series forecasting, achieving new state-of-the-art results across five benchmarks [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have introduced TempoWave, a novel multi-wavelet digit embedding method designed to enhance large language models (LLMs) for time series forecasting. TempoWave transforms scalar numerical observations into digit-wise embeddings using multi-scale wavelet coefficients, improving the alignment between continuous numerical data and the discrete tokenization processes of LLMs. This approach preserves numerical precision and digit identity while capturing both local fluctuations and global patterns in a form compatible with transformer architectures.
