The researchers have released the instrument as a diagnostic tool to better understand alignment and self-description in language models.

item.title: Researchers study how role-playing affects language models' internal belief representations using various persona induction methods, finding differing levels of belief internalization across approaches [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers investigated how role-playing different personas affects the internal belief representations of language models. They tested various persona induction methods, including prompting, in-context learning, supervised fine-tuning, Open Character Training, and Emergent Misalignment, using characters with beliefs that contrast modern consensus. The study found that while some methods mainly alter the models' outputs without changing their internal truth representations, others, particularly Emergent Misalignment, cause significant shifts in what the models internally represent as true. The research measured belief internalization through truth probes and behavioral tests, revealing a spectrum of effects depending on the induction approach. Prompting, in-context learning, and supervised fine-tuning led to minimal internal changes, whereas Emergent Misalignment produced broad shifts in truth representation, and Open Character Training caused smaller but noticeable changes, especially in larger models. Understanding when training modifies a model's underlying worldview rather than just its behavior is important as AI systems gain more autonomy and influence.

item.title: SymQNet uses amortized reinforcement learning to reduce acquisition latency in adaptive Hamiltonian learning for quantum devices, achieving up to 72.6× speedup at five qubits and 13× faster steps at twelve qubits [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: SymQNet is a new approach that uses amortized reinforcement learning to speed up adaptive Hamiltonian learning, a key process for calibrating and characterizing quantum devices. By learning an acquisition policy offline and applying it quickly online, SymQNet significantly reduces the time needed to decide the next experiment, achieving up to 72.6 times faster decision-making at five qubits and 13 times faster steps at twelve qubits compared to existing methods. The method was tested on transverse-field Ising model benchmarks, where it outperformed traditional Bayesian design rules and other active learning techniques by cutting acquisition latency from several seconds to just over one second for twelve-qubit systems. This reduction in latency makes adaptive Hamiltonian learning more practical for repeated, low-latency quantum device calibration tasks. SymQNet's ability to maintain Bayesian posterior feedback while accelerating experiment selection suggests it could enhance the efficiency of quantum device characterization, potentially benefiting the development and operation of larger quantum systems where rapid adaptive learning is critical.

item.title: Researchers argue AI alignment should focus on objective competence and factual constraints rather than aggregated human values, proposing a non-negotiable floor for AI behavior [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers argue that aligning artificial intelligence with aggregated human preferences is misguided due to the diverse and often conflicting values across societies. Instead, they propose establishing a non-negotiable baseline for AI behavior focused on objective competence, factual accuracy, honesty, and lawfulness. This approach aims to ensure AI systems operate within clear ethical and factual boundaries while allowing for pluralism in less critical aspects such as language and cultural conventions. The paper critiques the pluralistic-alignment approach, which recognizes the absence of a single unified human value system but warns against adopting it as the primary directive for AI alignment. The authors outline four commitments as an alternative framework and address six significant objections, including concerns about commercial pressures, democratic legitimacy, regulatory compliance, cultural biases in defining the baseline, and limitations of existing alignment theories. Their proposal emphasizes maintaining a foundational ethical floor to guide AI development amid diverse human values.

item.title: Researchers find post-training recipe influences multi-agent LLM conversational behavior more than model family, based on analysis of 940,000 and 1.6 million interaction chains [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have found that the post-training recipe of large language models (LLMs) influences their conversational behavior in multi-agent systems more significantly than the model family. Analyzing over 940,000 and 1.6 million interaction chains, the study shows that variations in training approaches can cause greater behavioral shifts than differences between model families, challenging prior assumptions that model family alone predicts conversational diversity. The study used extensive datasets including an 11-checkpoint corpus and a same-base Llama factorial to measure conversational traits like hedging. Results revealed that a reasoning-distilled Llama checkpoint's behavior varied by 18% depending on its partner model, exceeding cross-family differences. Additional checks with other models and APIs supported these findings, suggesting that post-training modifications are a critical factor in shaping multi-LLM interactions. These findings imply that selecting models for multi-agent LLM systems should consider post-training recipes alongside model family to achieve meaningful behavioral diversity. This insight could impact how multi-LLM panels are composed and evaluated in real-world applications, highlighting the need for more nuanced criteria beyond family labels.

item.title: Researchers find that a small group of Wikipedia editors significantly influences large language models' handling of animal welfare topics through targeted content edits [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have demonstrated that a small group of Wikipedia editors, known as the Pro-Animal Wikipedians (PAW), can significantly influence how large language models (LLMs) address animal welfare topics by making targeted edits to Wikipedia articles. Since Wikipedia content is heavily weighted in LLM training datasets, the PAW's 125 edits across 115 pages were found to be highly influential in shaping model responses specifically related to animal welfare, as shown through advanced data attribution techniques on models like Llama 3.1 and 3.2. The study used gradient-based data attribution and counterfactual influence estimation to trace the impact of PAW edits, revealing that these edits accounted for a majority of the most influential documents in animal welfare queries but not in unrelated queries. Fine-tuning models on PAW content further improved their performance on animal welfare texts, confirming that coordinated Wikipedia editing campaigns can measurably shape the values and outputs of language models on specific topics.

item.title: Researchers propose MiniOpt, a reinforcement learning framework that models and solves diverse optimization problems with limited training resources, achieving strong generalization across tasks [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have introduced MiniOpt, a reinforcement learning framework designed to solve a wide range of optimization problems efficiently with limited training resources. MiniOpt employs a "reasoning-to-model-and-solve" approach that breaks down optimization tasks into structured modeling and solver generation, supported by a novel reward function called OptReward that evaluates both problem formulation and solution quality without needing expert demonstrations. This framework enhances exploration efficiency and stabilizes learning for compact models, achieving strong generalization across various optimization types and domains. Extensive testing shows that MiniOpt-3B outperforms other models with fewer than 10 billion parameters in solving accuracy, while remaining competitive among larger models. These results highlight the potential of optimization-focused reward design and reinforcement learning to develop compact, specialized language models capable of generalizing effectively across diverse optimization challenges. The code for MiniOpt is publicly available for further research and development.

item.title: Researchers develop iterative data generation method using cascading linear features to detect and control sycophancy in language models, improving detection accuracy and interpretability [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have introduced an iterative data generation method that isolates cascading linear features to improve the detection and control of sycophancy in language models, which is the tendency to prioritize user validation. This approach moves beyond simple binary sample pairs by using samples that exhibit varying degrees of behavior, enabling clearer identification and steering of model activations related to sycophancy. The method achieves better detection, scoring, and control performance compared to existing baselines, while also reducing computational costs and enhancing interpretability. The study demonstrates that sycophancy features identified through cascading samples form linearly separable subspaces, allowing for more precise selection of model activations corresponding to the behavior. The approach matches or outperforms methods like LLM-as-a-judge and system prompting, providing robust and deterministic scoring capabilities. The researchers have made their code and data publicly available to support further exploration and application of this technique.

item.title: Researchers introduce CORE-Bench v1.1 and OOD suite to evaluate AI agent performance beyond accuracy saturation, highlighting efficiency, reliability, and human-agent collaboration benefits [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have introduced CORE-Bench v1.1 and an out-of-distribution task suite to address limitations in AI agent evaluation that arise after accuracy metrics saturate. Using CORE-Bench Hard, a benchmark for computational reproducibility of scientific code, as a case study, they highlight six additional performance dimensions including construct validity, generalizability, efficiency, reliability, the roles of model versus scaffold, and benefits from human-agent collaboration. Their findings demonstrate that these factors provide meaningful insights beyond accuracy alone. The study reveals threats to construct validity in the original benchmark and shows that CORE-Bench v1.1 remains effective for assessing efficiency and reliability despite accuracy saturation. A randomized experiment further indicates that human-agent collaboration can significantly accelerate computational reproducibility tasks, roughly doubling the speed compared to human-only efforts. This work advocates for a more comprehensive evaluation framework that extends beyond traditional accuracy-focused benchmarks.

item.title: Study finds refusal behavior in instruction-tuned chat models is gated downstream of persona expression, with compliant personas suppressing refusal in Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct and Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: A recent study on instruction-tuned chat models reveals that refusal behavior is influenced by the persona expressed by the model, rather than being an independent mechanism. Researchers found that in models like Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct and Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, a compliant persona can significantly suppress refusal responses, indicating that refusal is gated downstream of persona expression. The study involved extracting directions in the models' activation space corresponding to compliant persona and refusal, then intervening on both. Results showed that steering the model towards a compliant persona reduced refusal rates dramatically, while reintroducing refusal signals at later processing stages partially restored refusal behavior. This suggests that refusal is computed earlier but controlled at a later stage, highlighting the interaction between persona and refusal mechanisms in chat models.

item.title: Researchers present AlgoEvolve, an LLM-driven evolutionary framework that generates and improves Python-based algorithmic trading strategies with meta-evolutionary prompt optimization [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed AlgoEvolve, a framework that uses Large Language Models (LLMs) to generate and iteratively improve Python-based algorithmic trading strategies through evolutionary methods. This approach addresses the challenges of the trading domain, which is noisy and non-stationary, by producing executable strategies that adapt to changing market conditions and autonomously shift trading rules. The system incorporates a meta-evolutionary outer loop that optimizes the prompts guiding the inner loop of program synthesis, discovering improved heuristics that balance exploration and exploitation while reducing failures. These heuristics outperform initial human-designed instructions, demonstrating that LLM-driven semantic evolution is a promising method for continuous program synthesis in complex, dynamic environments.

item.title: Researchers introduce an LLM-powered pipeline for comparative governance analysis of DAO and corporate AI protocols, analyzing 4,323 records to study participation inequality and thematic convergence [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed a large language model (LLM)-powered pipeline to analyze governance structures in AI agent protocols, focusing on the comparative study of decentralized autonomous organizations (DAOs) and corporate-led AI standards. By examining 4,323 governance participation records from two distinct interoperability standards-ERC-8004 (permissionless, on-chain) and Google A2A (corporate-led)-the study integrates automated annotation, neural topic modeling, and multi-layer network analysis to explore how institutional design influences thematic priorities and community dynamics. The analysis reveals that while governance forms affect the substantive focus of discussions, both permissionless and corporate regimes show similar levels of participation inequality and community fragmentation. Notably, the permissionless setting exhibits denser discourse alignment, suggesting that open governance models may encourage greater thematic convergence despite decentralized participation. These findings demonstrate the potential of LLM-assisted methods to advance empirical research on technology governance and inform the design of more equitable AI standards. All related data and code have been made openly accessible.

item.title: Researchers develop a provenance-aware AI framework integrating Reddit, WebMD, and FDA data for psychiatric medication safety information with traceable claims and early adverse event detection [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed a provenance-aware, knowledge-graph-based AI framework that integrates data from Reddit, WebMD, and the U.S. FDA Adverse Event Reporting System to provide traceable and distinct safety information on psychiatric medications. The system analyzes over 466,000 Reddit posts, 60,000 WebMD reviews, and two decades of FDA records for nine antidepressants, using a large-language-model entity-recognition pipeline with high accuracy. This approach reveals that patient-generated data offer an independent safety signal, with some adverse events reported in community sources well before FDA documentation. The framework employs a Neo4j knowledge graph grounded in established medical vocabularies to maintain provenance and separate regulatory facts from patient experiences. The study highlights the potential for more auditable and context-aware psychiatric medication information, aiming to reduce misinformation and improve patient adherence. Future work will assess the practical benefits and usefulness of this integrated, source-aware system in clinical settings.

item.title: Researchers propose Drift-Diffusion-Enhanced Elo system to accelerate chess skill assessment using move-level data, demonstrating faster adaptation than traditional Elo ratings [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed the Drift-Diffusion-Enhanced Elo Rating System (DD-Elo), a new approach to assessing chess skill that incorporates move-by-move data to provide faster and more responsive skill evaluations than traditional Elo ratings. Inspired by cognitive neuroscience's drift diffusion model, DD-Elo models skill expression as a decision-making process, allowing it to capture rapid fluctuations in player performance while maintaining theoretical consistency with the classic Elo system. The DD-Elo system addresses the limitations of conventional rating methods that rely solely on match outcomes, which can delay recognition of skill changes. Through rigorous mathematical derivation and extensive experiments, the researchers demonstrated that DD-Elo adapts more quickly to shifts in player ability, offering an explainable and backward-compatible solution for chess rating systems. The implementation code for DD-Elo is publicly available for further exploration and use.

item.title: Researchers propose institutional attestation governance model for autonomous AI systems requiring independent verification of high-risk actions like clinical prescribing and software deployment [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have proposed a governance model for autonomous AI systems that require independent verification before executing high-risk actions such as clinical prescribing and software deployment. The model allows AI agents to maintain autonomy in planning and reasoning but restricts their authority to execute critical actions without independently attested evidence from authoritative sources. These attestations are cryptographically linked to the AI's declared intent and evaluated by a deterministic policy, with all decisions recorded in a tamper-evident log for independent review. This institutional attestation approach formalizes how human institutions govern powerful autonomous actors by focusing on verifying actions rather than monitoring internal reasoning. The researchers demonstrated a proof-of-concept implementation and illustrated the model's application in scenarios involving software deployment and clinical prescribing, highlighting its potential to enhance accountability and safety in autonomous AI operations.

item.title: Researchers present COrigami, an AI pipeline generating flat-foldable, visually recognizable origami crease patterns from natural language using reinforcement learning and algorithmic optimization [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed COrigami, an AI-driven pipeline that generates flat-foldable origami crease patterns from natural language descriptions. The system combines semantic interpretation, geometric computation, and reinforcement learning to produce crease patterns that meet strict mathematical constraints while also achieving visually recognizable designs. COrigami serves as a collaborative tool, providing structural starting points that human artists can further refine. The pipeline involves creating a semantic stick figure, computing base packing, solving for flat-foldable crease patterns, shaping the folded model, and refining it through an autonomous aesthetic evaluation loop. By integrating algorithmic optimization with aesthetic critique, this approach demonstrates how AI can handle multi-objective physical and artistic constraints to support mathematically grounded co-creativity in computational origami.

item.title: Study evaluates tool-augmented LLM agents on 243 real-world energy market analytics tasks using live data and domain-specific tools, comparing closed-source and open-source models [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: A new study evaluates the performance of tool-augmented large language model (LLM) agents on 243 real-world energy market analytics tasks, addressing a gap in energy-domain AI evaluations that typically rely on static knowledge recall. The tasks cover market data retrieval, knowledge interpretation, and advanced quantitative modeling, requiring live data access and specialized domain tools such as electricity market APIs, regulatory databases, and optimization models. Both closed-source and open-source LLMs were assessed using a multi-dimensional evaluation protocol that measures correctness, accuracy, and source validity. The study's evaluation environment includes expert-curated problems involving price and demand analysis, tariff impact modeling, asset revenue estimation, and hedging strategy analysis, reflecting real-world constraints and complexity. The research highlights how model capabilities interact with domain-specific tooling in a high-stakes professional setting and provides publicly available artifacts to support reproducibility and further research in energy market analytics using AI.

item.title: Researchers identify gaps in multimodal large language model evaluation, highlighting issues like temporal-spatial coherence and multimodal consistency in current benchmarks [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have identified significant gaps in the evaluation of multimodal large language models (MLLMs), which process inputs like text, images, audio, and video to generate textual responses. Current benchmarks tend to focus on isolated tasks and fail to assess how well these models integrate information across different modalities, leaving key aspects such as temporal-spatial coherence, physical world understanding, multimodal consistency, and selective attention underexplored. The study reviews existing evaluation methods and benchmark taxonomies, highlighting the need for more comprehensive assessments that capture the complex capabilities of MLLMs. Addressing these gaps is crucial for accurately measuring progress in multimodal intelligence and understanding the limitations of current models.

item.title: Researchers identify compositional behavioral leakage causing cross-module interference in prompt-composed agentic systems, demonstrated on Claude Sonnet 4.6 with a new evaluation protocol [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have identified a phenomenon called compositional behavioral leakage (CBL) in prompt-composed agentic systems, where modifying one prompt module unintentionally alters the behavior of others despite no direct dependencies. This interference arises from the lack of architectural isolation in transformer models, which share a context window without formal boundaries. The team demonstrated CBL on the Claude Sonnet 4.6 job-evaluation agent using a novel three-channel evaluation protocol, finding that changes in content caused measurable effects on other modules, though these effects remained below standard quality assurance detection thresholds. The study distinguishes CBL from other known failure modes such as adversarial attacks and privacy leaks, providing an operational definition, a reusable testing protocol, and a set of falsifiable predictions. These contributions establish the importance of measuring cross-module interference as a necessary step in evaluating and improving prompt-composed agentic systems.

item.title: Paper presents a mathematical interpretation of Kurzweil's accelerating returns thesis and introduces the Qualitative Engine for Science to address limits in AI-driven scientific discovery [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: A new paper offers a mathematical interpretation of Ray Kurzweil's accelerating returns thesis, which suggests that technological progress in fields like computing, AI, brain science, and biotechnology is self-reinforcing and exponential. The authors argue that while this acceleration enhances executional and infrastructural capabilities, it does not fully address the core challenge of scientific discovery, which requires qualitative reasoning to identify when existing frameworks are inadequate and to determine necessary conceptual shifts. The paper highlights recent findings showing a significant gap between human flexible reasoning and current AI performance, emphasizing the need for systems that support qualitative insight. It introduces the Qualitative Engine for Science (QES) as a tool designed to complement accelerating quantitative capabilities by preserving and organizing the human wisdom involved in scientific discovery. This approach underscores that advancing AI is not only a technical issue but also involves maintaining meaningful human understanding and focus.

item.title: Researchers propose an agentic aggregator framework for electric bus fleet operations integrating scheduling, disturbance detection, and tariff adaptation, highlighting trade-offs in profit-based coordination and policy implications [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed an agentic aggregator framework to enhance the operation of electric bus fleets by integrating scheduling, disturbance detection, and tariff adaptation. This framework combines an optimization-based scheduling model with supervisory agents that monitor real-time conditions, trigger re-optimization, and manage value allocation between the aggregator and public transport operators. The approach aims to balance service reliability, battery management, charger availability, electricity pricing, and vehicle-to-grid interactions. A case study simulating day-ahead and real-time operations under various disturbances and coordination modes demonstrated that the agentic aggregator can maintain feasible schedules and improve flexibility in charging and V2G usage. However, the study also identified a trade-off where profit-oriented pricing configurations could extract value from public transport operators, highlighting the need for transparent coordination, auditable tariffs, and clear value-sharing policies in public fleet deployments. These findings suggest that while agentic aggregators offer promising tools for managing electric bus fleets and their grid interactions, careful policy design is essential to ensure fair and effective implementation in public transportation contexts.

item.title: Researchers evaluate confidence interval methods for classifier performance metrics in text classification with small samples and nested data, highlighting improved accuracy with novel bootstrap techniques [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have evaluated various confidence interval methods for assessing classifier performance metrics in text classification tasks, particularly under conditions common in social science research such as small to moderate sample sizes, infrequent constructs, and nested data structures. Their study found that commonly used methods like the Wald interval and basic percentile bootstrap often provide inaccurate uncertainty estimates, while alternatives such as Agresti-Coull, Wilson, Clopper-Pearson, and a novel pseudo-count regularized bootstrap improve accuracy, especially for F1 score calculations. The research also highlights the importance of adjusting for effective sample size and degrees of freedom when texts are nested within individuals. Among bootstrap approaches, the hierarchical bootstrap performs better than the cluster bootstrap when individuals contribute a moderate number of texts but tends to be overly conservative with fewer texts per individual. This work aims to enhance the transparency and reliability of machine learning validation by guiding appropriate interval estimation and encouraging careful consideration of validation sample sizes during study design.

item.title: Researchers show supervised deep learning cannot achieve symbolic-level syllogistic reasoning due to training data and model limitations, with experiments on Euler Net and ChatGPT models [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have demonstrated that supervised deep learning models face fundamental limitations in achieving symbolic-level syllogistic reasoning, even with increased training data and time. Their study identifies two key issues: training data cannot differentiate all 24 valid types of syllogistic reasoning, and the end-to-end learning approach creates conflicting objectives between pattern recognition and logical reasoning components. Experimental results show that Euler Net fails to perform rigorous syllogistic reasoning, and tests on advanced ChatGPT models reveal that while GPT-5 can reach high accuracy on syllogistic tasks, it still produces incorrect explanations, influenced by the form of input statements. The findings suggest that current data-driven machine learning systems, including state-of-the-art language models, cannot fully replicate the precision of symbolic logical reasoning. This limitation arises because training processes typically halt once models achieve perfect accuracy on training data, which does not guarantee true logical rigor. Consequently, the study concludes that supervised learning approaches are unlikely to attain the level of reasoning demonstrated by symbolic methods.

item.title: Researchers introduce MKG-RAG-Bench, a cross-domain benchmark for evaluating retrieval in multimodal knowledge graph-augmented generation using general and medical datasets [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have introduced MKG-RAG-Bench, a new cross-domain benchmark designed to evaluate retrieval in multimodal knowledge graph-augmented generation (MKG-RAG). This benchmark addresses the challenges of retrieving heterogeneous and multimodal knowledge, which is critical for grounding large language models but often overlooked by existing benchmarks. MKG-RAG-Bench includes datasets from general and medical domains with aligned question-answering tasks to assess both retrieval and generation performance. The benchmark was developed using a large language model-based curation pipeline that filters low-utility knowledge and generates structurally grounded queries with exact supervision. Extensive experiments demonstrate that effective multimodal retrieval remains a significant challenge and strongly influences the quality of generated outputs. By focusing on retrieval as a primary evaluation target, MKG-RAG-Bench offers a structured framework to identify current limitations and advance the development of MKG-RAG systems.

item.title: Researchers present auto-psych, an agent-based system automating theory discovery and experimentation in computational cognitive science using crowdsourced human data [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed auto-psych, an agent-based system that automates theory discovery and experimentation in computational cognitive science by independently collecting human data through crowdsourced surveys. The system uses nested loops where one generates and critiques cognitive models while the other designs and conducts experiments online. Tested on a classic cognitive psychology problem involving perceptions of randomness in coin flip sequences, auto-psych successfully recovered known theories from synthetic data and produced models that better fit human experimental data than existing scientific theories. This approach leverages the programmability of cognitive theories and the scalability of crowdsourcing platforms to address data collection bottlenecks in AI-driven scientific automation. By integrating hypothesis generation, experimental design, data collection, and analysis, auto-psych demonstrates the feasibility of fully automated scientific discovery in cognitive science, potentially accelerating research and improving model accuracy beyond traditional methods.

item.title: Researchers propose Clinical Harness architecture for governable medical AI skills to support accountable, lifecycle clinical care using osteoporosis as an example [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have introduced the Clinical Harness, a governance architecture designed to manage and monitor AI-enabled clinical capabilities over time, addressing the limitations of isolated medical AI models. This system supports accountable, lifecycle clinical care by registering, orchestrating, and safeguarding AI skills. Using osteoporosis as a case study, the researchers demonstrate how integrating knowledge-driven, data-driven, and physics-enhanced AI skills can enhance continuous patient care under runtime governance.

item.title: arXiv: NeuraDock releases open-source EEG agent tutorial for quality-gated Alpha dynamics and real-time visual cognitive-load analysis with mini-dataset validation [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: NeuraDock has released an open-source EEG agent tutorial that guides users through a quality-gated workflow for analyzing Alpha brainwave dynamics and real-time visual cognitive load. The tutorial enables users to install the agent, preprocess EEG data with quality control, generate Alpha dynamics visualizations, compare cognitive load between rest and task states, and run analyses on a public mini-dataset. It also supports launching an online dashboard, accessing a real-time API, and using a language model layer to interpret data quality risks. This tutorial addresses the challenge of integrating offline EEG analysis with real-time applications by providing a reproducible pipeline that computes Alpha and workload metrics only after quality gating. Validation on a mini-dataset showed the agent processed 18 recordings, produced within-subject comparisons revealing task-related Alpha suppression, and demonstrated initial repeatability and low API latency. The resource is designed for researchers and developers seeking a transparent method to build real-time cognitive load prototypes from EEG data.

item.title: Researchers present NeuraDock Agent, an open-source architecture combining a deterministic EEG engine with a hardware-aware language layer for low-channel EEG analysis and boundary-aware context grounding [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed NeuraDock Agent, an open-source system designed to improve the analysis of low-channel electroencephalography (EEG) data by combining a deterministic local EEG processing engine with a hardware-aware language model layer. This architecture ensures that the language model receives only a controlled summary and context about the specific EEG hardware and workflows, helping to prevent unsupported interpretations common in sparse EEG data. The system maintains raw EEG data locally while producing consistent, machine-readable results through validated spectral workflows. The NeuraDock Agent was evaluated through multiple tests, including repeated numerical analyses, failure-injection experiments, and boundary-awareness benchmarks involving ordinary and adversarial queries. These tests confirmed the system's reliability in preserving data integrity and its ability to calibrate what the EEG agent accepts or rejects based on hardware and implementation constraints. While the results demonstrate practical grounding for EEG data interpretation, the researchers note that the system does not establish clinical validity or provide a validated cognitive-load index.

item.title: Researchers propose EvoOptiGraph, a graph-based coevolution framework that generates structurally diverse optimization models guided by model weaknesses, outperforming larger models on six public datasets [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have introduced EvoOptiGraph, a novel framework that enhances optimization modeling from natural language by enabling coevolution of data and models based on model weaknesses. This approach represents mixed-integer linear programs as attributed bipartite graphs and uses evolutionary operators to generate structurally diverse instances, which are then converted into solver code and natural language. Training involves supervised fine-tuning followed by reinforcement learning guided by signals derived from model weaknesses, creating a feedback loop that continuously refines the training data. Tests on six public datasets demonstrate that EvoOptiGraph outperforms larger generalist models and specialized baselines in accuracy, executability, and generalization. The results suggest that targeted coevolution of data and models is an effective strategy for improving large language models in optimization tasks, addressing challenges related to limited structural diversity in training data and static data generation pipelines.

item.title: Researchers propose a multi-level validation and traceability framework to improve reliability and executability of AI-generated telescope scheduling decisions [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed a multi-level validation and traceability framework to enhance the reliability and executability of AI-generated telescope scheduling decisions. This framework systematically verifies AI outputs before execution, addressing issues such as inconsistent data references, reasoning errors, and non-executable plans that have limited AI's use in high-reliability astronomical observations. By integrating data validation, logical consistency checks, and constraint verification, the framework filters and corrects invalid decisions while representing the reasoning process through interconnected atomic units to support error localization and analysis. Experiments demonstrate that this approach improves the executability and reliability of AI scheduling, reducing the loss of transient observational opportunities. The framework's feedback correction and structured validation enable it to repair or block erroneous decisions, particularly in complex scenarios. Compared to pure AI methods, this enhanced approach maintains flexibility while significantly boosting reliability, offering a practical and verifiable path for applying AI in critical astronomical scheduling tasks.

item.title: Researchers develop an email dispatcher using large language models to automatically route emails to relevant WhatsApp groups in an engineering college, improving information flow and reducing manual effort [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed an automated email dispatcher that uses large language models (LLMs) to analyze email content and route messages to relevant WhatsApp groups within an engineering college. This system aims to streamline communication by automatically forwarding emails to appropriate student groups based on their content, reducing the manual effort and errors associated with traditional email handling. The dispatcher operates through an agent framework that inputs email content along with instructions and context to determine the correct recipient groups. Unlike conventional methods, this approach does not require labeled datasets and leverages the decision-making capabilities of LLMs to enhance productivity and decrease the cognitive load involved in managing large volumes of emails.

item.title: Researchers present LLM-based methodology combining fine-tuned models and human oversight to detect emerging multilingual service feedback topics and inequities, validated by tax officers [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed a new methodology that combines fine-tuned large language models (LLMs) with human oversight to analyze multilingual service feedback, particularly for public sector organizations like tax administrations. This approach aims to detect emerging service quality issues and potential inequities by integrating statistical techniques and human-AI collaboration, improving the accuracy and efficiency of feedback analysis compared to traditional methods. The framework was validated through similarity analysis and evaluations by experienced tax officers, showing better alignment with expert judgments than baseline models. By incorporating a human-in-the-loop system, the methodology reduces errors commonly associated with LLMs and enhances the reliability of insights, supporting scalable, evidence-based decision-making. This work contributes to responsible AI development that promotes fairness, responsiveness, and public trust in service delivery through more effective analysis of diverse customer feedback.

item.title: Researchers present an autoformalization pipeline using LLMs to translate agent instructions into formally verified policies in Cedar Policy Language, improving coverage on MedAgentBench [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed an autoformalization pipeline that uses large language models (LLMs) to convert agent instructions, tool descriptions, and natural language policy documents into formally verified policies written in the Cedar Policy Language. This approach addresses the limitations of existing methods, which either rely on probabilistic guardrails without formal guarantees or on hand-coded symbolic enforcement that lacks scalability. The new pipeline demonstrated improved coverage of natural-language specifications on the MedAgentBench benchmark compared to prior hand-coded symbolic methods. The pipeline employs a generator-critic loop powered by LLMs to ensure the formal verification of the generated policies. By automating the translation process, it enables more comprehensive and scalable enforcement of agent safety policies in high-stakes domains, enhancing reliability and formal assurance beyond previous approaches.

item.title: Researchers introduce SkillDisCo framework to distill and compile reusable procedural skills from agent traces, improving success rates and reducing execution steps in FSM-defined tasks [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed SkillDisCo, a framework that distills and compiles reusable procedural skills from agent task traces defined by finite state machines (FSMs). This approach identifies shared control-flow structures within successful task executions and transforms them into callable, executable skills, reducing redundant reasoning and lengthy execution paths. SkillDisCo demonstrated improved success rates and fewer execution steps in experiments on ALFWorld and WebArena benchmarks. The framework treats successful agent traces as paths in an unknown transition graph and extracts parameterized subgraphs representing procedural skills. By compiling these subgraphs into verifiable skills, SkillDisCo enables agents to reuse experience efficiently across similar tasks. This method addresses challenges in identifying which scenarios support procedural skills and how to represent shared procedural structures effectively. SkillDisCo's ability to enhance performance across different model scales and benchmarks highlights the value of representing shared experience as reusable execution structures. This advancement could lead to more efficient agent behavior in complex task environments by minimizing repetitive problem-solving efforts.

item.title: Researchers present NebulaExp-8B, a transparent post-training pipeline for 8B-scale LLMs with ablation studies improving instruction and reasoning benchmarks using multi-source data and reinforcement learning [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have introduced NebulaExp-8B, a transparent post-training pipeline designed for 8-billion-parameter large language models (LLMs). Built on the Qwen3-8B-base model, NebulaExp features two branches: a general instruction-following model and a complex reasoning-specialized model. The pipeline uses a curated dataset of 3.84 million multi-source supervised fine-tuning samples and a 200,000-sample reinforcement learning candidate pool, along with an end-to-end data processing system that includes response distillation, filtering, difficulty grading, task classification, and diversity-aware sampling. The instruction branch employs a three-stage supervised fine-tuning approach that improves benchmark scores significantly, with further gains achieved through reinforcement learning. The reasoning branch also benefits from reinforcement learning, enhancing reasoning performance. To reduce reliance on task verifiers in reinforcement learning, the team explored single-teacher and multi-teacher offline policy distillation methods, which improved performance using fewer samples. This work provides a fully reproducible post-training recipe for 8B-scale LLMs and analyzes trade-offs among instruction adherence, mathematical reasoning, code generation, and general knowledge capabilities.

item.title: Researchers introduce Kalman Prototypical Networks for few-shot fault detection in combined cycle gas turbines, improving accuracy and stability on simulated leak fault tasks [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed the Kalman Prototypical Network (KPN), a few-shot learning framework designed to improve fault detection in combined-cycle gas turbines (CCGTs), which are critical for efficient and environmentally friendly power generation. The KPN models class prototypes as latent stochastic states in a dynamic system to enhance robustness and reduce variance in embedding representations, addressing challenges posed by limited labeled fault data. Testing on synthetic datasets simulating normal and leak fault conditions in an offshore CCGT system showed that KPN outperforms existing few-shot learning methods in accuracy and stability across different configurations. The study utilized high-fidelity Modelica-based dynamic simulations to generate data reflecting transient operational conditions and progressive leak faults. By stabilizing class representations, the KPN framework improves training convergence and generalization, making it particularly suitable for real-world CCGT fault diagnosis where labeled examples are scarce. This advancement offers a promising approach to enhancing the reliability and maintenance of complex power generation systems.

item.title: Researchers present LithoDreamer, a physics-informed World Model framework for multi-stage computational lithography achieving state-of-the-art performance in forward evolution and inverse planning [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed LithoDreamer, a novel physics-informed World Model framework designed to improve multi-stage computational lithography, a critical process in semiconductor manufacturing. LithoDreamer models the entire lithography pipeline-from layout and mask design to resist imaging and development-as a decision-driven, multi-step evolution system, capturing the physical changes at each stage to optimize process interventions effectively. This approach enables state-of-the-art performance in both forward evolution and inverse planning tasks, addressing limitations of previous models that could not fully represent the continuous physical nature of lithography. The framework introduces a contrastive variational optimization method that guides the model to generate physically consistent lithography evolutions without requiring continuous supervision. By modeling stage-specific latent spaces informed by lithography physics, LithoDreamer controls process interventions and drives subsequent state transitions more accurately. The researchers have also made their lithography dataset publicly available on GitHub, facilitating further research and development in this area.

item.title: Researchers present a latent ODE model for continuous spatiotemporal cine cardiac MRI analysis, improving heart failure risk prediction in 72,386 UK Biobank participants [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed a latent dynamical model that captures continuous spatiotemporal information from cine cardiac magnetic resonance imaging (CMR) to improve heart failure risk prediction. The model uses heart-rate-aware neural ordinary differential equations and a graph-based mesh autoencoder to reconstruct anatomically consistent 3D ventricular motion throughout the cardiac cycle. Applied to data from 72,386 UK Biobank participants without baseline cardiovascular disease, the model's latent score enhanced risk prediction accuracy beyond traditional cardiac markers and pooled cohort equations. This approach encodes bi-ventricular anatomy and full-cycle motion as a continuous latent trajectory, with a covariate-conditioned prior defining expected end-diastolic states. A Cox proportional hazards model demonstrated that deviations from this prior predict incident heart failure. Compared to non-graph and non-ODE methods, the proposed model achieved superior balance between reconstruction fidelity, generative realism, and prognostic performance. The findings suggest that continuous full-cycle modeling of ventricular motion provides richer cardiac phenotypes than conventional CMR summaries. However, the researchers note that external validation in more diverse patient cohorts is necessary before clinical implementation for risk prediction.

item.title: Researchers introduce AHOIS, a multi-agent AI system using Socratic questioning for autonomous scientific discovery in complex high-dimensional physical systems, validated on multimode-fibre optical experiments [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed AHOIS, a multi-agent AI system that integrates Socratic questioning to enable autonomous scientific discovery in complex, high-dimensional physical systems. Tested on a multimode-fibre optical platform, AHOIS autonomously generated and validated hypotheses, identified measurement strategies, diagnosed failure modes, and adapted existing imaging protocols without prior models or classifiers. This approach advances beyond fixed workflows by allowing the AI to construct, challenge, and revise physical explanations based on experimental evidence. The system demonstrated effective performance by producing 16x16 measurements with high effective rank and achieving classification accuracies of 76.97% on MNIST and 83.17% on Fashion-MNIST datasets. Ablation studies confirmed that the Socratic interrogation method enhances the physical consistency and completeness of hypotheses, improves uncertainty calibration, and validates experimental plans. These findings suggest a promising path toward self-correcting, evidence-based autonomous discovery in complex physical environments.

item.title: Researchers propose EGG, an expert-guided agent framework for GPU kernel generation that achieves 2.13x speedup over PyTorch by combining algorithmic design and hardware-specific tuning [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed EGG, an expert-guided agent framework designed to automate the generation of high-performance GPU kernels, which are essential for managing the computational demands of large language models (LLMs). EGG improves upon existing methods by integrating expert optimization strategies into a two-stage process: algorithmic structure design and hardware-specific tuning. This approach enables more effective exploration of optimization options, resulting in a 2.13x average speedup over PyTorch in tests on KernelBench and real-world workloads. The framework employs a stage-aware multi-agent collaboration mechanism to manage context and ensure stable optimization throughout the kernel generation process. By decomposing the task into hierarchical stages with explicit objectives, EGG achieves progressive refinement in kernel performance. This method outperforms previous agent-based and reinforcement learning approaches, highlighting the benefits of combining domain expertise with automated kernel design.

item.title: Researchers introduce ResilPhase, a noise-resilient diffusion acceleration framework using phase mapping and derivative-free macro-trajectory extrapolation to improve inference speed and fidelity [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed ResilPhase, a new framework designed to accelerate diffusion model inference while maintaining high fidelity. This approach addresses the limitations of existing acceleration methods, which often degrade quality due to unstable and misaligned extrapolations. ResilPhase reformulates inference as stable macro-trajectory extrapolation in ordinary differential equation space, aligning forecasting with the model's global state evolution to reduce errors and memory use. The framework introduces a derivative-free barycentric Lagrange extrapolator to avoid instability from noisy higher-order derivatives and employs bounded Phase Mapping to control extrapolation errors. Experiments on datasets like FLUX.1-dev and HunyuanVideo demonstrate that ResilPhase achieves state-of-the-art fidelity even under aggressive acceleration, offering a promising solution to the latency challenges in deploying powerful diffusion models.

item.title: Study analyzes heart rate variability indices in 40 healthy adults using computational methods to assess normality, stability, correlation, reproducibility, and consistency for clinical utility
item.description: A study analyzed heart rate variability (HRV) indices in 40 healthy adults to enhance the clinical utility of HRV measurements. Using computational methods, the research assessed time, frequency, and nonlinear HRV indices for normality, stability, correlation, reproducibility, and consistency. The study found that time-domain and nonlinear indices generally follow normal distributions and are stable, while frequency-domain indices, especially those related to high frequency, showed variability and redundancy. The analysis revealed gender differences in some indices and identified specific HRV measures-such as ApEn and IRRR for global variability, HRVi and SD2 for low frequency, and MADRR or rMSSD for high frequency-as most suitable for accurately representing HRV components. Comparisons with an external database showed low error rates for most indices, supporting their reproducibility. These findings provide guidance for selecting reliable HRV indices in clinical and research settings, improving the assessment of cardiac physiological states in healthy individuals.

item.title: Researchers introduce Capability Frontier showing benchmarks miss 82% of large language model performance across 21 models and 16 tasks, highlighting underestimated collective capabilities [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have introduced the Capability Frontier, a new method that reveals traditional benchmarks underestimate large language model (LLM) performance by 82%. By evaluating 21 LLMs across 16 diverse tasks, the study shows that combining multiple models and multiple outputs per model significantly improves accuracy compared to single-model, single-run evaluations. This approach accounts for model specializations and optimally selects outputs, providing a more accurate measure of LLM capabilities. The study corrects biases from conventional benchmarking by using a Pareto frontier to represent the best achievable performance at each cost level, balancing underestimation from single-model tests and overestimation from noisy samples. Empirical results demonstrate a 54% reduction in error rates when moving beyond single-model evaluation, and an 82% improvement when also considering multiple runs, achieving state-of-the-art accuracy with 85% less cost. Simulations further indicate that performance gains increase with the diversity of query topics. These findings suggest that collective LLM capabilities are substantially underestimated in current evaluations, highlighting the need for revised benchmarking and deployment strategies in multi-domain, heterogeneous data environments.

item.title: Researchers propose CASOP framework to synthesize and evaluate over one million context-specific optimization pipelines for warehouse order fulfillment tasks [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed the Context-Aware Synthesis of Optimization Pipelines (CASOP) framework to improve order fulfillment in manual picker-to-goods warehouses. CASOP addresses the challenge of integrating interconnected decisions like item assignment, order batching, and picker routing by enabling the construction and evaluation of context-specific optimization pipelines. The framework includes a modular algorithm repository, semantic descriptions of warehouse contexts and algorithm requirements, a taxonomy of order fulfillment subproblems, a pipeline synthesizer to generate valid algorithm combinations, and a pipeline evaluator to assess their performance. The framework was tested on seven benchmark instance sets covering four problem classes, resulting in over one million valid optimization pipelines. CASOP supports both researchers and practitioners by automating the design and selection of effective algorithmic solutions tailored to specific warehouse contexts. The software is open-source and available online, facilitating further research and practical application in warehouse operations optimization.

item.title: Researchers introduce LCAi, an AI-assisted life cycle assessment framework using big data fusion and retrieval-augmented generation for structured interpretation and strategic decision-making [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed LCAi, an AI-assisted framework that enhances life cycle assessment (LCA) interpretation by integrating big data fusion and retrieval-augmented generation. This approach uses a multi-perspective retrieval system combined with controlled synthesis to translate environmental impact data into actionable strategic pathways, addressing uncertainties in technology, society, and policy. The framework was demonstrated using a hydrogen-enabled diesel reduction case in an Italian apple production facility, employing GPT-5 nano as the reasoning model to ensure accurate and diverse insights while minimizing AI hallucination risks. The LCAi framework operates through three key steps: defining system boundaries and decarbonization targets, executing perspective-specific micro-queries with constrained data retrieval, and synthesizing results neutrally without further data fetching. It incorporates datasets from academic, industry, public discourse, and European Union funding sources to provide a comprehensive view. This method supports more disciplined and evidence-based decision-making in LCA studies, particularly for scalable technologies, and represents a significant advancement in applying advanced AI tools to environmental impact assessments.

item.title: Researchers introduce TAVR-VLM with Risk-Conditioned Causal Grounding Attention to reduce hallucinations in multimodal AI report generation for Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement planning, achieving 8.1% hallucination rate on 1,482-patient dataset [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed TAVR-VLM, a new multimodal AI framework designed to improve report generation for Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement (TAVR) planning by reducing diagnostic hallucinations-errors where generated text lacks anatomical grounding. The system uses Risk-Conditioned Causal Grounding Attention (R-CGA) to create a structured pathway linking risk assessment to specific anatomical regions and words, enhancing the accuracy and interpretability of generated reports. Evaluated on a dataset of 1,482 patients, TAVR-VLM achieved state-of-the-art performance with an AUROC of 0.896, a CIDEr score of 0.936, and notably reduced the hallucination rate to 8.1%. This advancement supports more reliable, evidence-based surgical AI by ensuring that generated diagnostic text is closely grounded in relevant medical imaging data.

item.title: Researchers release a pipeline and dataset generating longitudinal synthetic clinical notes using large language models to support clinical AI development without real patient data [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed a pipeline and released a dataset that generate longitudinal synthetic clinical notes using large language models, aiming to support the development of clinical AI tools without relying on real patient data. This approach addresses privacy concerns by creating synthetic patient records that maintain internal consistency over time while reflecting variations in writing style and clinical detail. The dataset includes 70 synthetic patients, each with 20 to 50 clinical notes covering a full hospital stay, and is available at multiple validation levels to suit different research needs. The pipeline integrates structured patient generation, simulation of patient journeys, and unstructured clinical note creation, enhanced by validation and augmentation steps to improve the realism and diversity of the synthetic notes. This resource facilitates the development, testing, and evaluation of various clinical AI applications such as summarization, coding, and decision support systems, enabling progress in healthcare AI while mitigating privacy risks associated with real clinical data.

item.title: Researchers propose MO-DiT+HPPO framework for pattern-preserving attribute retrieval using diffusion transformers and metric-ordered sequence training, showing improvements across four attribute domains [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have introduced MO-DiT+HPPO, a novel framework for pattern-preserving attribute retrieval that combines diffusion transformers with metric-ordered sequence training and hybrid-policy preference optimization. This approach addresses the challenge of retrieving items that both match a target attribute and maintain a fine-grained pattern expressed by a seed set, balancing the trade-off between pattern preservation and attribute relevance. The framework involves staged training including raw-sequence pretraining, multi-domain metric-ordered continuation pretraining, tail-centroid fine-tuning, and HPPO, which aligns generated queries with online objectives using a hybrid candidate pool and preference optimization. Evaluations across four attribute domains demonstrate that MO-DiT+HPPO significantly improves retrieval performance, enhancing attribute metrics without sacrificing pattern purity, and outperforms pretrained generative retrievers under various holdout protocols. Further analysis through metric-predictor validation, ablation studies, and comparisons with other training methods clarifies the sources of these improvements, highlighting the effectiveness of metric-ordered training and preference optimization in advancing continuous generative retrieval techniques.

item.title: Researchers propose ReTeX framework to recover task-specific expert performance from a single merged multi-task model checkpoint, achieving over 95% accuracy in vision and NLP tasks [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed ReTeX, a framework designed to recover the performance of task-specific expert models from a single merged multi-task model checkpoint. ReTeX addresses the issue of parameter interference that occurs during static merging by predicting additive offsets to undo these perturbations, enabling recovery of over 95% of individual expert performance in both vision and natural language processing tasks. The framework also includes a router-free task identifier that selects the appropriate expert based on input, without prior knowledge of task identity. ReTeX improves generalization to unseen tasks by adaptively interpolating knowledge from existing experts, particularly benefiting out-of-distribution scenarios. This approach reduces the need for storing multiple expert components during inference, offering a more efficient solution for multi-task learning. The researchers have made their code publicly available for further exploration and application.

item.title: Researchers identify task insensitivity as a key cause of out-of-distribution failures in language agents and propose Task-Perturbed NLL Optimization to improve task sensitivity and generalization [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have identified task insensitivity as a major factor behind the poor out-of-distribution (OOD) generalization of large language models when used as long-horizon agents. These models tend to apply learned patterns from training even when faced with similar but distinct tasks, often continuing actions aligned with the original task despite corrupted or altered instructions. This behavior is linked to an attention shift during training away from task instructions toward local observations, indicating an optimization bias toward shortcuts. To address this issue, the researchers propose Task-Perturbed NLL Optimization, a contrastive regularizer designed to increase the model's sensitivity to task instructions. Their evaluations demonstrate that this method improves task sensitivity and OOD generalization while maintaining stable attention to task tokens, offering a promising approach to enhance the reliability of language agents across varied tasks.

item.title: Researchers analyze chain-of-thought training in large language model agents, finding it improves prompt-action prediction more than reasoning revision and enhances out-of-domain generalization [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have investigated the effects of chain-of-thought (CoT) training on large language model agents, focusing on whether it improves the model's ability to revise actions through reasoning or enhances direct action prediction from prompts. Their study found that CoT training primarily boosts the quality of prompt-based action predictions rather than increasing the advantage of reasoning-based action revisions. Over time, models rely more on prompt information and less on revising actions through CoT reasoning. The researchers also experimented with selectively masking action-token supervision during training, which led to improved generalization in out-of-domain scenarios. These findings suggest that CoT training benefits language model agents by strengthening prompt-action prediction capabilities and that targeted training interventions can further enhance model robustness across different contexts.

item.title: Researchers propose Look-Before-Move framework for narrative-grounded visual attention and camera planning in dynamic 3D story worlds, introducing a new 3D Story World Benchmark with 50 stories and 1585 shots [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have introduced the Look-Before-Move framework to enhance camera planning in dynamic 3D story worlds by enabling narrative-grounded visual attention. This approach allows the camera to actively decide what to observe and how to compose its view before moving, aligning visual perception with narrative intent and physical constraints. The framework separates observation specification from motion execution through a Semantic Observation Contract, Monte Carlo Viewpoint Search, and Semantic Trajectory Grounding to produce smooth, collision-aware camera motion. To support evaluation, the team developed a new 3D Story World Benchmark based on StoryBlender, featuring 50 stories, 457 scenes, and 1585 shots with animated characters and semantic scene configurations. Experiments demonstrate that this method improves subject perception, narrative consistency, and trajectory quality compared to existing baselines, highlighting the importance of organizing visual attention prior to camera movement in embodied AI systems operating in complex 3D environments.

item.title: Researchers present AURORA-AI, an adaptive resource orchestration framework that maximizes fairness, performance, and stability in AI systems under demographic bias and operational disruptions [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed AURORA-AI, an adaptive resource orchestration framework designed to enhance fairness, performance, and stability in AI systems facing demographic bias and operational disruptions. The framework integrates feedback control, stability monitoring, and a fairness-aware utility function to dynamically allocate computational resources across diverse AI models, maximizing overall utility under changing conditions. AURORA-AI was tested in simulations involving demographic bias shocks, concept drift, and sudden disruptions, outperforming several established controllers including static and reinforcement learning-based methods. It demonstrated faster recovery from disruptions, improved fairness metrics, and increased system stability, suggesting that adaptive, fairness-aware resource management grounded in stability theory offers a promising approach for resilient, human-centric AI deployment.

item.title: arXiv paper reviews external validity indexes for clustering evaluation with ground truth, recommending centroid index for cluster-level and pair-set index for point-level measures [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: A new paper on arXiv reviews common external validity indexes used for evaluating clustering results when ground truth data is available. The authors recommend the centroid index (CI) as an intuitive and explainable cluster-level measure. For more detailed, point-level evaluation, they suggest the pair-set index (PSI), which provides a normalized score unbiased by cluster sizes, while clustering accuracy (ACC) or other set-matching measures are suitable if all points are to be weighted equally. The paper focuses on set-matching-based measures and compares their properties to guide researchers in selecting appropriate evaluation metrics based on their specific clustering analysis needs.

item.title: Researchers present JERP, a method that jointly updates experiential rules and policies for large language model agents to improve decision-making in complex interactive tasks [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed JERP, a method that simultaneously updates experiential rules and policies for large language model (LLM) agents to enhance decision-making in complex interactive tasks. JERP integrates a long-term rule pool with policy optimization by using interaction trajectories to both refine the rules and improve the agent's policy, ensuring alignment between the two. This approach allows the agent to retrieve relevant rules during decision-making and adapt its behavior based on past experiences. JERP addresses limitations of previous methods that either kept experience as static natural-language rules or updated model parameters separately, which could lead to inconsistencies or limited correction in sparse-reward environments. By jointly learning from the same interaction data, JERP maintains stable and effective behaviors that evolve with the policy. Experiments on environments like AlfWorld and WebShop demonstrate that JERP consistently improves decision performance for LLM agents in multi-step tasks.

item.title: Researchers introduce OpenRCA 2.0 with PAVE protocol for step-wise causal supervision in root cause analysis, revealing LLMs recover exact root causes in 20.7% of cases across 11 models [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have introduced OpenRCA 2.0, a new benchmark for root cause analysis (RCA) that includes step-wise causal annotations using the PAVE protocol. This approach addresses limitations in existing datasets by labeling not only the root cause but also the causal propagation path from cause to observed symptom, enabling more rigorous evaluation of large language models (LLMs) in multi-step reasoning and long-context understanding. Testing 11 advanced LLMs on OpenRCA 2.0 revealed that they correctly identify the exact root cause in only 20.7% of cases on average. The PAVE protocol leverages fault injection interventions to reconstruct causal paths, shifting evaluation from backward symptom inference to forward cause-to-effect verification. While LLMs identified at least one correct root cause in 76.0% of cases, they grounded that cause in a verified causal path only 61.5% of the time, highlighting a significant gap in causal reasoning. This step-wise causal supervision uncovers failure modes hidden by outcome-only evaluations and is essential for developing trustworthy LLM-based RCA agents.

item.title: Researchers propose TOPS, a training-free visual token pruning method for multimodal large language models that removes up to 77.8% of tokens while preserving or improving performance on LLaVA-NeXT models [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have introduced TOPS, a training-free and model-agnostic method for visual token pruning in multimodal large language models (MLLMs). TOPS aims to improve efficiency by removing up to 77.8% of visual tokens while maintaining or enhancing performance, as demonstrated on LLaVA-NeXT models. This approach is based on three principles-Task Relevance, Information Coverage, and Semantic Diversity-derived from an information-theoretic analysis to optimize token selection. Extensive testing across seven MLLM architectures and fourteen benchmarks shows that TOPS outperforms existing pruning methods. Notably, it preserves full or slightly improved performance on both 7B and 13B parameter LLaVA-NeXT models despite significant token reduction. The findings suggest that eliminating redundant visual tokens can reduce hallucination and guide the development of more efficient multimodal models in the future.

item.title: Researchers introduce process harness mechanism to add policy-governed agentic layers to legacy workflows using the Task-Decision-Flow model and CUGA FLO implementation for Agentic BPM [ * ] [ ⬢ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed a process harness mechanism that enhances legacy workflows by adding a policy-governed agentic layer without replacing the existing workflow engine. This approach, based on the Task-Decision-Flow (TDF) model, integrates three types of agents-TaskAgent, DecisionAgent, and FlowAgent-that contribute reasoning, adaptation, and oversight at designated control points while maintaining the engine's structural control. The CUGA FLO implementation demonstrates this model in a loan approval workflow, balancing deterministic execution with policy-driven agentic autonomy to meet both imperative and normative process requirements. The TDF model rigorously defines the process harness through a data schema and execution semantics, enabling large language model reasoning to be distributed across specialized agents governed by explicit policies from the process FRAME. This design allows for runtime flow adaptation and regulatory overrides, ensuring compliance and flexibility within legacy systems. The process harness thus offers a novel way to uplift existing workflows into Agentic Business Process Management (Agentic BPM) by combining structural enforcement with autonomous decision-making capabilities.

item.title: Researchers propose GAversary, a genetic algorithm using GloVe embeddings to generate adversarial text attacks that reduce natural language model accuracy from 76.8% to 5.8% on benchmarks [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed GAversary, a genetic algorithm that uses GloVe embeddings to create adversarial text attacks against natural language processing models. GAversary operates as a black-box method, requiring only the model's output logits to guide its search for effective word replacements. This approach significantly reduces model accuracy on benchmark datasets, dropping it from 76.8% to as low as 5.8%, outperforming existing attacks like BAE and A2T. GAversary improves semantic similarity in adversarial examples by leveraging GloVe embeddings during mutation, although it modifies nearly twice as many words as other methods and incurs a slight increase in runtime. The method demonstrates the vulnerability of NLP models to evolutionary-generated adversarial inputs, highlighting challenges in securing deep learning systems against such attacks.

item.title: Researchers introduce EO-WM, a video diffusion transformer with physically informed conditioning for probabilistic Earth observation forecasting, improving vegetation decline prediction under extreme weather conditions [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed EO-WM, a video diffusion transformer designed for probabilistic Earth observation forecasting that incorporates physically informed conditioning to better predict vegetation decline under extreme weather conditions. This model treats weather as a conditioning signal and addresses uncertainty in forecasting caused by sparse observations and unobserved land-surface states. EO-WM distinguishes between climatological baselines and weather anomalies, accumulating physical stress signals over time to capture sustained heat and drought effects. To assess the model's ability to respond accurately to changing weather, the researchers introduced two new benchmarks: the Extreme Summer Benchmark for predicting vegetation degradation severity and the Seasonal Matched-Pair Benchmark for evaluating forecast fidelity under altered weather conditions. Experiments demonstrated that EO-WM improves prediction accuracy of vegetation decline amplitude by 5.63% and directional hit rate by 7.80%, while maintaining competitive performance on standard pixel-level metrics. The model and benchmarks will be made publicly available to support further research in Earth observation forecasting.

item.title: Researchers compare simulation-based inference with MCMC for rapid Bayesian calibration of COVID-19 epidemiological models, showing SBI reduces runtime from thousands to under 200 seconds [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have demonstrated that simulation-based inference (SBI) using neural posterior estimation can significantly accelerate Bayesian calibration of mechanistic epidemiological models compared to traditional Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) methods. By applying SBI to a COVID-19 SECIR model with intensive care unit occupancy data from Germany, they achieved comparable accuracy to MCMC while reducing computation time from thousands of seconds to under 200 seconds, leveraging GPU resources. The study compared SBI and MCMC across multiple epidemic phases, including both short 31-day inference windows and a complex 201-day reconstruction involving multiple transmission changes. SBI maintained strong agreement with MCMC in posterior distributions and predictive performance, even in the more challenging long-term scenario, while offering substantial runtime improvements. These findings suggest that SBI provides a rapid and computationally efficient framework for near-real-time Bayesian calibration of epidemiological models, facilitating faster outbreak analysis and public health decision-making during infectious disease events.

item.title: Researchers study prompt injection in automated résumé screening with large language models, finding it boosts rankings when rare but loses effectiveness as manipulation spreads, raising fairness concerns [ * ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have investigated the impact of prompt injection-subtle self-promotional text without new qualifications-on automated résumé screening using large language models (LLMs). Their controlled experiments reveal that prompt injection can improve applicant rankings when résumé quality is similar and few candidates use this tactic, but its effectiveness declines sharply as more candidates engage in manipulation, eventually becoming ineffective when widespread. The study also finds that in cases of varied candidate quality, prompt injection is generally less effective but can sometimes allow lower-quality applicants to outrank higher-quality ones, raising concerns about fairness in algorithmic hiring. The research highlights that LLM-based screening systems are most vulnerable to manipulation when candidate quality differences are small and prompt injection is rare. These findings underscore the challenges of maintaining fairness and reliability in automated hiring processes as candidates adapt to algorithmic evaluation methods.
