The authors have made their code and resources publicly available to support further study in this area.

item.title: Researchers propose language-based digital twins using large language models to mimic elderly conversational behavior for cognitive health monitoring, showing comparable accuracy to real data on I-CONECT dataset [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed a language-based digital twin framework that uses large language models to replicate the conversational behavior of elderly individuals, aiming to support cognitive health monitoring. By integrating stylometric features and contextual metadata, the system models individual speech patterns to detect early signs of Mild Cognitive Impairment (MCI). Evaluation on the I-CONECT dataset demonstrated that these digital twins maintain identity-specific traits and achieve prediction accuracy for cognitive scores comparable to real data, outperforming standard GPT-generated responses. The approach employs a multi-head conditional variational autoencoder to assess both the quality of conversation reconstruction and cognitive score prediction, highlighting its potential as a scalable, non-invasive tool for personalized and continuous monitoring of cognitive health in older adults.

item.title: Researchers benchmark four open-weight language models on Global AI Dataset v2 to assess geographic bias and accuracy disparities across 227 countries from 2010 to 2023 [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers evaluated four open-weight large language models using the Global AI Dataset v2 to investigate geographic bias and accuracy differences across 227 countries from 2010 to 2023. The study addresses limitations of previous research by using publicly available models, focusing on data within the models' training periods, and employing a detailed five-category classification of model responses to distinguish between accurate answers, confident fabrications, and other response types. The analysis involved approximately 2,990 observations across 18 indicators aligned with the IEEE IRAI 2026 framework, applying mixed-effects logistic regression and difference-in-differences methods to assess disparities. This approach provides a more rigorous and transparent assessment of how geographic representation in training data affects model performance in AI governance contexts.

item.title: Paper analyzes legal and technical risks of AI-generated music under US copyright law, highlighting gaps in protection for synthesized vocal likeness and implications of recent cases and legislation [ * ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: This paper explores the legal and technical challenges of AI-generated music under U.S. copyright law, focusing on the use of copyrighted lyrics, AI-composed melodies, and synthetic vocals that imitate real artists. It examines whether creating and monetizing songs using protected lyrics combined with AI-generated voices or styles infringes on exclusive rights under Title 17 of the U.S. Code. The analysis highlights that unauthorized lyric use likely violates musical composition rights, while AI-generated voice imitation generally falls outside federal sound recording protections and is instead governed by state publicity laws. The study reviews recent court cases and legislation, such as Concord v. Anthropic and Tennessee's "ELVIS Act," to illustrate the current legal landscape. It also maps AI technical components like prompt encoding and neural vocoders to associated legal risks, identifying a regulatory gap where federal law protects lyrics and melodies robustly but offers limited remedies for synthesized vocal likeness. The paper concludes with policy recommendations aimed at clarifying rules for AI music creation.

item.title: arXiv: Study examines generative AI's impact on creative industries, highlighting OpenAI's Sora model release, audience quality limits on AI content, UK copyright tensions, and major studios' AI strategies [ * ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: A new study analyzes the transformation of creative industries driven by generative artificial intelligence, focusing on the December 2024 release of OpenAI's Sora video model as a pivotal moment. The research introduces the Human-AI Agency Continuum to map collaboration between humans and AI in creative work and identifies an audience-imposed "slop ceiling" limiting AI-generated content to 1-3% of platform streams despite making up 44% of uploads. It also highlights tensions revealed by the UK Government's 2025 consultation on AI and copyright, where most respondents opposed expanded AI training rights. The study examines how major studios like Disney and Netflix are adapting to AI-augmented production pipelines, including Disney's $1 billion investment in OpenAI and Netflix's AI-native animation unit. It discusses challenges such as coordination breakdowns in creative supply chains and the emergence of new roles like prompt engineers and AI orchestrators. The authors propose four guiding principles for the industry's transition: transparency, consent, compensation, and human-centered design, supported by extensive quantitative analysis and supplementary materials.

item.title: Researchers propose a multi-layer AI framework for analyzing information landscapes across reliability, bias, framing, and propagation to support nuanced media analysis and information disorder research [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed a multi-layer AI framework designed to analyze information landscapes in the context of information disorder. Unlike traditional misinformation detection that focuses on binary fact-checking, this framework evaluates political and media content across various dimensions such as source reliability, factual structure, framing, bias, emotional activation, manipulation patterns, and propagation dynamics. The approach aims to provide a structured representation of the informational environment surrounding events, entities, or narratives, supporting a more comprehensive understanding beyond isolated claims. The framework emphasizes epistemic mapping, offering a transparent, multi-dimensional view of how facts, interpretations, actors, and narratives interact over time. The paper outlines the conceptual architecture, analytical layers, and methodological rationale behind this approach, aiming to facilitate more nuanced, explainable, and critically useful tools for research into information disorder and media analysis.

item.title: Study finds ChatGPT and Claude disagree on two-thirds of brand recommendations but converge on diagnosing failure modes 95% of the time across 7,763 joint failures [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: A study analyzing product recommendations from ChatGPT and Claude found that the two AI providers disagree on brand recommendations about two-thirds of the time. However, when neither recommends a brand, they diagnose the failure mode-categorized as discoverability, compellingness, or positioning-in agreement 95% of the time across 7,763 joint failures. This high concordance in failure diagnosis increases as brand prominence decreases, reaching nearly complete agreement for less prominent regional brands. The research highlights that ChatGPT and Claude use different generative approaches to make recommendations but converge on identifying why brands fail to be recommended, especially for the long tail of less prominent brands. Addressing these diagnosed failure modes improves brand visibility on both platforms, though strategies for category leaders require more provider-specific efforts focused on positioning and content.

item.title: Researchers propose Governance Inversion Hypothesis, arguing increased AI regulation may reduce organisational control by fragmenting authority and complicating oversight [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have proposed the Governance Inversion Hypothesis (GIH) to address a paradox in AI governance: as regulatory measures increase and AI systems grow more complex, organizations may become more formally governed yet lose operational control over these systems. Contrary to the common belief that stronger regulation enhances accountability and oversight, the hypothesis suggests that expanding governance structures can fragment authority and complicate effective management of AI technologies. The study draws on institutional theory and governance research to identify four mechanisms-authority fragmentation, symbolic governance expansion, externalization of control, and authority paralysis-that contribute to this erosion of control. As governance frameworks become more layered and procedural, organizations may face challenges in maintaining clear authority, technical insight, and the ability to intervene meaningfully in AI operations. The paper warns that the main risk in AI governance may not be a lack of regulation but the emergence of complex institutions that appear well-governed while actually diminishing their capacity to govern effectively.

item.title: Researchers propose privacy-aware multi-agent reinforcement learning framework for dynamic VR slice management in 6G SD-RAN, improving throughput by 34% and reducing privacy leakage by 85% in simulations [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed a privacy-aware multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) framework to manage dynamic virtual reality (VR) slices in 6G Software-Defined Radio Access Networks (SD-RANs). This approach aims to optimize resource allocation for VR services, ensuring ultra-low latency and high throughput while safeguarding user data privacy. Simulations demonstrate that the framework improves throughput by up to 34%, reduces resource usage by 28%, and decreases privacy leakage by 85% compared to traditional methods. The framework integrates mobility prediction and an information bottleneck encoder to enable effective and secure collaboration among cooperative agents managing end-to-end VR links. These innovations address the critical challenges of dynamic resource management in future 6G networks, supporting reliable and immersive VR experiences.

item.title: Researchers propose Geo-FairFed, a geometric fairness-aware routing system using hyperbolic graph neural networks and federated optimization to improve latency, energy use, and fairness in 6G and IoT edge networks [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed Geo-FairFed, a routing system designed for emerging 6G and edge-intelligent networks that integrates hyperbolic graph neural networks with federated optimization to enhance latency, energy efficiency, and fairness across distributed edge devices. This approach models network topologies on a negatively curved manifold to capture hierarchical and asymmetric connections, while a global aggregator enforces fairness by minimizing routing loss and inequality based on Jain's fairness index. The system aims to balance performance equitably among nodes rather than focusing solely on aggregate metrics. Theoretical analysis confirms convergence under certain curvature constraints and demonstrates that the fairness component leads to a Pareto-improving equilibrium in routing outcomes. Simulations on dynamic 6G-edge and IoT network topologies show that Geo-FairFed reduces average latency by 20%, cuts energy consumption by 17%, and improves fairness by up to 21% compared to existing federated and geometric routing protocols. These results suggest that embedding network topology in hyperbolic space and incorporating fairness into federated learning can significantly improve the efficiency and equity of large-scale network routing.

item.title: Researchers develop multiscale model coupling strategic exit-join decisions with tactical consensus dynamics to analyze coalition formation and stability in multi-agent systems
item.description: Researchers have developed a multiscale model that integrates strategic decisions to exit or join coalitions with tactical consensus dynamics within those coalitions. This model generates coalition value through internal information aggregation and uses Aumann-Dreze payoffs, switching frictions, and acceptance rules to guide coalition restructuring. The framework features a fast-slow architecture where transferable coalition value arises from consensus processes, while coalition structures evolve based on incentive-driven exit and join behaviors. The study characterizes equilibria involving both tactical and strategic factors, identifying conditions for unanimity, segregation, polarization, and cognitive barriers that maintain stable coalitions. It establishes fixed-point characterizations and existence results for the coupled dynamics. Numerical experiments reveal an instability-consensus paradox, where low or negative switching barriers can hinder strategic convergence but promote sufficient temporal mixing to achieve global tactical consensus. These findings offer a unified perspective on coalition formation, consensus dynamics, information aggregation, and strategic stability in multi-agent systems, advancing understanding of how complex group behaviors emerge and persist.

item.title: Researchers introduce Video Memory Transformers for unsupervised real-time obstacle detection on autonomous agricultural rover, achieving state-of-the-art results on rapeseed dataset [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed Video Memory Transformers for Anomaly Detection (VMTAD), an unsupervised method designed to detect obstacles in real-time for autonomous agricultural rovers. This approach addresses the limitations of traditional sensors like LiDAR, which cannot detect obstacles beneath plant canopies, and supervised camera-based methods that struggle with unseen obstacles. VMTAD uses a transformer architecture with a memory module that processes temporal context from previous frames, enabling effective detection in dynamic environments without requiring labeled data. The system was tested on the 'Grillion' agricultural rover using a challenging rapeseed dataset, achieving state-of-the-art results with detection and segmentation AUC scores of 0.973 and 0.997, respectively. A lightweight version of VMTAD balances high accuracy with real-time inference speed of 14 milliseconds, which is crucial for ensuring the rover's operational safety by allowing timely obstacle detection and response.

item.title: Researchers propose ARReST method to reduce redundancy in whole-slide image patching, achieving 3% to 60% storage savings while maintaining retrieval accuracy across 21 organs in TCGA dataset [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed ARReST (Antithetical Redundancy Reduction Strategy), a new method designed to reduce redundancy in whole-slide image (WSI) patching for digital pathology. ARReST targets patches that contribute little to distinguishing between different tissue classes, pruning them to significantly decrease the number of patches indexed without compromising retrieval accuracy. This approach addresses the high storage costs associated with WSI indexing, which is critical for supporting retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) workflows in clinical decision-making. Testing on The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA) dataset, which includes images from 21 organs, demonstrated that ARReST can achieve storage savings ranging from 3% to 60% while maintaining competitive retrieval performance. By reducing unnecessary patch representations, ARReST lowers storage requirements and computational overhead, enabling faster similarity searches and more scalable, cost-effective indexing of large pathology image repositories. This method holds promise for enhancing the efficiency of next-generation clinical AI systems reliant on retrieval-driven workflows.

item.title: Researchers propose LCG framework with Sparse Relational Attention for consistent long-context multi-image generation, introducing a large synthetic dataset with 600K sequences [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have introduced Long-Context Generation (LCG), a new framework designed to improve consistency in multi-image text-to-image generation over extended sequences, which is crucial for applications like comics and storyboards. LCG uses Sparse Relational Attention (SRA) to efficiently focus on key features across long visual contexts and employs a Routing Consistency Constraint (RCC) to maintain semantic alignment and reduce appearance drift, even in complex scenes with multiple characters. To support this work, the team created the Long-Context Consistency Dataset (LCCD), a large synthetic dataset with 600,000 training sequences and 1,000 test sequences, each containing 6 to 20 images. Experiments demonstrate that LCG outperforms existing methods in maintaining prompt alignment and character consistency across long image sequences. The introduction of SRA and RCC mechanisms enables scalable and coherent generation, addressing challenges in long-context multi-image synthesis and advancing the quality of visual narrative generation.

item.title: Researchers present CyberChainBench, a benchmark evaluating LLM-based AI agents on smart contract security using 541 real-world exploits across 9 EVM chains with detection, exploitation, and patching tasks [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have introduced CyberChainBench, a comprehensive benchmark designed to evaluate large language model (LLM)-based AI agents on smart contract security. The benchmark covers three key tasks: vulnerability detection, exploit generation, and patch synthesis, using data from 541 real-world exploits across nine Ethereum Virtual Machine (EVM) chains. CyberChainBench enables end-to-end on-chain evaluation by allowing agents to interact with historical blockchain states in isolated environments, assessing their ability to identify vulnerabilities, generate exploits, and create effective patches.

item.description: Lacuna is a research mapping tool for machine learning that leverages large language models to convert academic papers and metadata into structured markdown summaries, concept elements, research directions, and proposals, all linked to their original sources. It offers web, markdown, and MCP interfaces and demonstrates superior performance compared to OpenScholar, particularly in retrieval tasks such as LitSearch. This advancement highlights Lacuna's potential to improve the organization and accessibility of machine learning research.

item.title: Researchers develop multi-task spatiotemporal deep neural network predicting penetration depth and weld seam morphology in laser welding with over 99% accuracy [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed a multi-task spatiotemporal deep neural network that predicts penetration depth, penetration state, and weld seam morphology in laser welding with high accuracy. Using weld pool images captured by a complementary metal-oxide-semiconductor camera during the welding process, the model combines spatial and temporal features with welding parameters through convolutional neural networks and state space models. This approach enables efficient extraction and processing of spatial-temporal information for quality assessment. The study also introduces a reliable dataset construction method to improve the model's robustness and generalization. Validation results show the model achieves 99.35% accuracy in predicting penetration state, a penetration depth error of 1.79 millimeters, and 95.65% accuracy in reconstructing the weld cross-section. These findings offer new methodologies for in-situ quality control in laser penetration welding systems.
